docs.title: Crackz
docs.text: AI-powered crack detection and analysis for harbor and bridge infrastructure.

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Crackz is a commercial-grade crack detection solution designed for infrastructure inspection. Reduce inspection costs by up to 70% while improving safety and consistency through automated AI-powered analysis.

New to Crackz? Start with the Getting Started Guide to be up and running in minutes.

Ready to install? Check out the Installation Guide for setup instructions.

docs.title: For Infrastructure Managers
docs.text:
• Reduce costs – Process thousands of images in hours instead of weeks
  • Improve safety – Minimize physical inspections in hazardous locations
  • Early detection – Identify structural issues before they become critical
  • Proven ROI – Typical savings of $25,000-$75,000 annually per inspection program

docs.title: For Technical Teams
docs.text:
• Reproducible projects – Self-contained folder structure for complete traceability
  • Fast experimentation – Runtime overrides for rapid iteration
  • Scriptable & visual – Powerful CLI plus modern GUI
  • Container friendly – Docker images for all deployment scenarios
  • Extensible design – Modular AI pipeline built on PyTorch Lightning

docs.title: Model Capabilities
docs.text:
Crackz uses deep learning segmentation models to identify cracks at the pixel level:

  • Binary segmentation: Detect crack/no-crack with precise pixel masks
  • Multi-class segmentation: Identify multiple defect types (cracks, corrosion, spalling)
  • Flexible encoders: Choose from 20+ backbones (ResNet, EfficientNet, MobileNet, etc.)
  • Transfer learning: Leverage pre-trained ImageNet weights for better accuracy

docs.title: Two Deployment Paths
docs.text:
1. Use Pre-Trained Models (Fastest) - Quick deployment with ready-made checkpoints - Standard crack detection scenarios - Consistent results across sites

2. Train Custom Models (Most Accurate) - Domain-specific imagery and unique defect types - Maximum accuracy for your infrastructure - Requires labeled training data (images + masks)

See the Getting Started Guide for detailed workflows.

docs.text: Category Capabilities Interfaces CLI (crackz) and GUI (crackz-gui) for all workflows Data Management Structured splits (raw/train/val/test) with automatic organization AI Pipeline Segmentation models with configurable encoders and metrics Logging Hybrid central + project logs for complete audit trails Configuration Pydantic-validated YAML configs with schema versioning Deployment Local, Docker (CPU/GPU), Azure Batch, standalone executables Training Runtime overrides for rapid experimentation

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
Every Crackz project is self-contained with complete traceability:

my-project/
├── images/           # Source images by split (raw/train/val/test)
├── masks/            # Ground truth for training
├── artifacts/        # Detection results and training metrics
├── logs/             # Complete audit trail
└── project.yaml      # Configuration snapshot

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
# Create project
crackz init --name demo

# Import images
crackz import-images --project demo --src ./photos --type raw --size 512 512

# Run detection
crackz detect run --project demo

# View results in demo/artifacts/detections/

Or use the GUI: 

crackz-gui
# File → New Project → Import Images → Run Detection

docs.title: Advanced Performance & Reproducibility
docs.text: This page describes optional settings for faster training / inference and more reproducible runs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Advanced knobs live under ai.training and ai.detection in the project YAML (or unified ProjectConfig). They are all optional and default to safe, CPU‑friendly values.

Area Field Location Purpose Precision precision ai.training Mixed precision / bfloat16 acceleration Devices devices ai.training Number of devices (GPUs) for distributed training Strategy strategy ai.training PyTorch Lightning strategy (e.g. ddp) Reproducibility seed ai.training, ai.detection Sets global RNGs (python/numpy/torch/lightning)

docs.title: Mixed Precision
docs.text:
Mixed precision can significantly improve throughput on modern GPUs.

Supported values (Lightning compatible): - 16 or 16-mixed – FP16 mixed precision - bf16-mixed – bfloat16 mixed precision (Ampere + some CPUs) - 32 – (default if omitted)

Example: 

ai:
  training:
    precision: 16-mixed
    batch_size: 16
CLI run: 
crackz detect train --project demo-project
(Precision is read from project YAML; no extra flag required.)

docs.title: Multi-GPU / Distributed Training
docs.text:
Enable multi-GPU training by specifying devices > 1 and a suitable strategy (usually ddp).

ai:
  training:
    devices: 2
    strategy: ddp
    batch_size: 8
    precision: bf16-mixed

Run (assuming 2 visible GPUs): 

crackz detect train --project demo-project

Docker (GPU): 

docker run --gpus all --rm -v %cd%\project:/home/app crackz-cli:gpu \
  detect train --project /home/app/demo-project

docs.title: Strategies Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Strategy Use Case Notes ddp Standard multi-GPU Best default on Linux ddp_spawn Windows / Jupyter Slight overhead auto Let Lightning decide Conservative choice

docs.title: Seeding & Reproducibility
docs.text:
Set seed in either training or detection sections: 

ai:
  training:
    seed: 1234
  detection:
    seed: 1234
Effect: - Sets PYTHONHASHSEED, python random, numpy, torch (CPU + CUDA), and Lightning worker seeds. - Does NOT force deterministic convolution algorithms (can slow performance). Add those manually if needed: 
import torch
torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• GPU kernels may still introduce nondeterminism (atomic ops, etc.).
  • Different hardware / driver stacks can still change results slightly.

docs.title: Example Comprehensive YAML
docs.text:
project:
  name: demo-project
  description: Perf tuned
paths:
  project_path: demo-project
  image_path: demo-project/images
  image_mask_path: demo-project/masks
  artifacts_path: demo-project/artifacts
logging:
  level: INFO
  log_dir: logs
ai:
  model:
    encoder: resnet34
    device: cuda
    input_size: [512, 512]
    threshold: 0.5
  training:
    batch_size: 16
    epochs: 20
    learning_rate: 0.0005
    precision: 16-mixed
    devices: 2
    strategy: ddp
    seed: 4242
  detection:
    batch_size: 8
    seed: 4242

docs.title: Workflow Tips
docs.text: Goal Tip Prototype quickly Keep CPU defaults; small batch, epochs=1, precision unset Throughput Increase batch_size gradually; enable 16-mixed precision Large model memory Use bf16-mixed (if supported) or reduce batch_size Reproducible baseline Fix seed; export config (crackz export-config)

docs.title: Exporting a Tuned Config
docs.text:
After modifying fields inside the project YAML: 

crackz export-config --project demo-project --out tuned_config.yaml
Share tuned_config.yaml for reproducible runs.

docs.title: Detection Phase Seeds
docs.text: Providing ai.detection.seed ensures preprocessing ordering / transforms (if later added) are deterministic between runs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Suggestion OOM errors Lower batch_size or remove mixed precision Slower than expected Ensure CUDA visible; confirm precision active in logs DDP hang Use ddp_spawn on Windows or for notebook contexts Seed ineffective Check for non-deterministic ops; set torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This page documents the core Python interfaces for programmatic use of Crackz.

Tip: All high‑level tasks (init, import-images, detect, train) are available via the CLI, but you can also call them directly from Python for integration into notebooks, pipelines, or custom services.

docs.title: Load a Project & Run Detection
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from crackz.project.project import load_project_from_path
from crackz.ai.detection import detect

project = load_project_from_path(Path("demo-project"))
# Optional: custom progress reporter
progress = lambda p, msg=None: print(f"{p:.0%}", msg or "")

detect(project, progress_reporter=progress)

project = load_project_from_path("demo-project")

docs.title: Create a New Project Programmatically
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from crackz.project.project import (
    ProjectMetadata, ProjectPaths, create_project, save_project
)

project = create_project(
    metadata=ProjectMetadata(name="demo-project", description="Example"),
    paths=ProjectPaths(
        project_path=Path("demo-project"),
        image_path=Path("demo-project/images"),
        image_mask_path=Path("demo-project/masks"),
        artifacts_path=Path("demo-project/artifacts"),
    ),
    force=False,
)
save_project(project)

docs.title: Settings (Environment / YAML)
docs.text:
CrackzSettings supports environment overrides with the prefix CRACKZ_ (e.g. CRACKZ_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG).

A module for managing and loading project configuration.

This module provides a configuration model and functionality to load the configuration from a YAML file.

Exceptions:

This module contains exception classes related to configuration errors.

The exceptions defined here are used to handle various errors that occur during the configuration or project lifecycle process, such as missing configuration files or invalid configuration content.

docs.title: CrackzSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSettings

Configuration for a ai crackz project.

Source code in src/crackz/config/crackz_settings.py 
class CrackzSettings(BaseSettings):
    """Configuration for a ai crackz project."""

    name: str = "crackz_project"
    log_dir: Path = Path("logs")
    log_level: str = "INFO"

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_file=".env",
        env_prefix="CRACKZ_",
        case_sensitive=False,
    )

    @classmethod
    def from_conf(cls, conf_file: Path) -> "CrackzSettings":
        """
        Creates and returns an instance of the class from a configuration file.
        This method reads a YAML configuration file from the given file path, parses
        its content into a dictionary, and uses it to initialize and return an
        instance of the class.

        If the configuration file is empty, an empty dictionary will be used.
        If the file does not exist, FileNotFoundError is raised.
        :param conf_file: Path or str pointing to the YAML file.
        :return: A new instance of the class initialized with the configuration
                 data from the file.
        :rtype: CrackzSettings
        """
        if not conf_file.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {conf_file!s}")

        try:
            with conf_file.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
            return cls(**data)

        except FileNotFoundError as e:
            raise ConfigFileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {conf_file!s}") from e
        except yaml.YAMLError as e:
            raise InvalidConfigError(f"Error parsing YAML configuration {conf_file!s}: {e}") from e
        except Exception as e:
            raise ConfigError from e

docs.title: Unified Project Configuration (Scaffold)
docs.text:
A minimal serializable wrapper combining model/training/detection/logging settings.

Unified ProjectConfig scaffold.

This provides a light-weight configuration model that can be serialized independently of the full Project instance. It wraps the component models already defined in project.project and adds helper factory methods to construct a Project or persist the config.

Minimal by design - extend with additional global settings later (e.g. random seeds, mixed precision flags, registry URIs, feature toggles).

docs.title: ProjectConfig
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Serializable project configuration wrapper (minimal).

Source code in src/crackz/config/project_config.py 
class ProjectConfig(BaseModel):
    """Serializable project configuration wrapper (minimal)."""

    name: str
    description: str = ""
    project_path: Path
    image_path: Path
    image_mask_path: Path
    artifacts_path: Path
    logging: LoggingConfig = LoggingConfig()
    model: ModelConfig = ModelConfig()
    training: TrainingConfig = TrainingConfig()
    detection: DetectionConfig = DetectionConfig()

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> ProjectConfig:
        """Load the configuration from the given path."""
        data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return cls(**data)

    def save(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Save the configuration to the given path."""
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            yaml.safe_dump(self.model_dump(mode="json"), f, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True)

    def to_project(self) -> Project:
        """Construct a ``Project`` from this ``ProjectConfig``."""
        return Project(
            project=ProjectMetadata(name=self.name, description=self.description),
            paths=ProjectPaths(
                project_path=self.project_path,
                image_path=self.image_path,
                image_mask_path=self.image_mask_path,
                artifacts_path=self.artifacts_path,
            ),
            logging=self.logging,
            ai=AIConfig(
                model=self.model,
                training=self.training,
                detection=self.detection,
            ),
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_project(cls, project: Project) -> ProjectConfig:
        """Construct a ``ProjectConfig`` from a ``Project``."""
        return cls(
            name=project.project.name,
            description=project.project.description,
            project_path=project.paths.project_path,
            image_path=project.paths.image_path,
            image_mask_path=project.paths.image_mask_path,
            artifacts_path=project.paths.artifacts_path,
            logging=project.logging,
            model=project.ai.model,
            training=project.ai.training,
            detection=project.ai.detection,
        )

docs.text:
Project objects encapsulate paths, metadata, and convenience helpers.

A set of utility functions and classes to manage and manipulate project configurations.

This module provides functionality to create, configure, save, and manage project-related directories and metadata. It is optimized to handle common scenarios during project setup, including directory creation and YAML-based serialization for project configurations. All project configurations follow a fixed structure to ensure consistency during usage.

It includes: - A Pydantic-based Project model to define project metadata. - Functions to generate required project directories. - Functionality to serialize project configurations to persistent storage in YAML format.

Supporting types:

Project-level constants.

Exceptions:

This module defines custom exception classes related to project operations.

These exception classes inherit from CrackzError and represent specific errors encountered in the context of projects, such as configuration issues or file import errors.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Represents a project model with configuration for storing project details.

The Project class encapsulates the essential attributes and configurations of a project. This includes details such as the project's name, description, creation date, and storage-related paths. Designed to work with a BaseModel-compatible configuration that ensures model extensibility. :

Source code in src/crackz/project/project.py 
class Project(BaseModel):
    """
    Represents a project model with configuration for storing project details.

    The Project class encapsulates the essential attributes and configurations of
    a project. This includes details such as the project's name, description,
    creation date, and storage-related paths. Designed to work with a
    BaseModel-compatible configuration that ensures model extensibility.
    :
    """

    project: ProjectMetadata
    paths: ProjectPaths
    logging: LoggingConfig
    ai: AIConfig
    data: DataConfig = DataConfig()  # Data preprocessing configuration
    schema_version: int | None = None  # Added for migration tracking

    model_config = {
        "ser_json_timedelta": "iso8601",
        "ser_json_bytes": "utf8",
    }

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The name of the project."""
        return self.project.name

    @property
    def config_file(self) -> Path:
        """The expected config file name for this project."""
        return Path(f"{self.project.name}{PROJECT_FILE_SUFFIX}")

    @property
    def detections_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the detected images data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the detected images data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.artifacts_path) / DETECTIONS_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def models_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the models directory (new structure).

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the models directory.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.artifacts_path) / MODELS_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def checkpoints_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the checkpoints directory.

        Deprecated: Use models_path instead. This property provides
        backward compatibility by checking for legacy 'checkpoints'
        directory and falling back to new 'models' directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the models directory (or legacy checkpoints for old projects).
        """
        warnings.warn(
            "checkpoints_path is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. "
            "Use models_path instead.",
            DeprecationWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        # For backward compatibility: if legacy checkpoints directory exists and models doesn't,
        # use the legacy directory. Otherwise use the new models directory.
        legacy_checkpoints_dir = Path(self.paths.artifacts_path) / CHECKPOINTS_DIR_NAME
        models_dir = self.models_path

        if legacy_checkpoints_dir.exists() and not models_dir.exists():
            return legacy_checkpoints_dir
        return models_dir

    @property
    def runtime_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the runtime directory for logs and temporary artifacts.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the runtime directory.
        """
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / RUNTIME_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def training_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the training directory."""
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / TRAINING_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def detections_visualizations_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the detection visualizations subdirectory."""
        return self.detections_path / VISUALIZATIONS_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def detection_results_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the training metrics JSON file."""
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / DETECTIONS_DIR_NAME / "detection_results.json"

    @property
    def training_metrics_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the training metrics JSON file."""
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / TRAINING_DIR_NAME / "training_metrics.json"

    @property
    def tensorboard_logs_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the TensorBoard logs directory (in runtime/)."""
        return self.runtime_path / "tensorboard"

    @property
    def lightning_logs_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the PyTorch Lightning logs directory (in runtime/)."""
        return self.runtime_path / "lightning_logs"

    @property
    def val_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model validation data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the validation data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / VAL_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def test_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model test data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the test data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / TEST_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def train_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model train data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the train data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / TRAIN_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def train_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model train mask data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the train data directory derived from the
                  provided image mask path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / TRAIN_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def val_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model validation mask data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the validation data directory derived from the
                  provided image mask path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / VAL_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def test_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model test mask data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the test data directory derived from the
                  provided image mask path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / TEST_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def raw_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the raw (detect) test data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the raw data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / RAW_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def raw_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the raw mask (detect) test data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the raw data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / RAW_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def project_file_path(self) -> Path:
        """Compute the path where the project YAML will be saved."""
        return Path(self.paths.project_path) / f"{self.project.name}{PROJECT_FILE_SUFFIX}"

    @property
    def _image_ops(self) -> ImageOperations:
        """Get ImageOperations instance with current project paths."""
        return ImageOperations(
            image_path=Path(self.paths.image_path),
            image_mask_path=Path(self.paths.image_mask_path),
            train_path=self.train_path,
            val_path=self.val_path,
            test_path=self.test_path,
            raw_path=self.raw_path,
            train_mask_path=self.train_mask_path,
            val_mask_path=self.val_mask_path,
            test_mask_path=self.test_mask_path,
            raw_mask_path=self.raw_mask_path,
            mask_threshold=self.data.mask_threshold,
        )

    def map_type_to_dir(self, image_type: ImagesType) -> Path:
        """
        Maps a given image type to its corresponding directory path.

        This method takes an image type as input and resolves it to a corresponding
        directory path. It supports types such as `raw`, `train`, `test`, and `val`.
        If the given value does not map to a valid type, the function defaults to the
        `raw` directory path.

        :param image_type: The type of the image to map ("raw", "train", "test", or "val").
        :return: The `Path` object representing the directory mapped from the given
                 image type, or `None` if no mapping exists.
        """
        return self._image_ops.map_type_to_dir(image_type)

    def map_type_to_masks_dir(self, image_type: ImagesType) -> Path:
        """
        Maps a given image type to its corresponding directory path.

        This method takes an image type as input and resolves it to a corresponding
        directory path. It supports types such as `raw`, `train`, `test`, and `val`.
        If the given value does not map to a valid type, the function defaults to the
        `raw` directory path.

        :param image_type: The type of the image mask to map ("raw", "train", "test", or "val").
        :return: The `Path` object representing the directory mapped from the given
                 image type, or `None` if no mapping exists.
        """
        return self._image_ops.map_type_to_masks_dir(image_type)

    def save_project(self) -> None:
        """
        Saves the given project to a file in YAML format. The function serializes
        the project data using the model's `model_dump` method, and writes it to
        a specified path. The path is determined dynamically based on the project
        information. Logging is performed to confirm success or log any errors
        encountered during the saving process.

        :param project: The project object to be saved. The project must implement
            the `model_dump` method for serialization.
        :return: None
        """
        try:
            path = self.project_file_path
            if self.schema_version is None:
                from crackz.project.migration import CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION

                self.schema_version = CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION

            # Update Crackz version on save to track last modification
            from crackz.version import get_version

            self.project.crackz_version = get_version()

            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                yaml.safe_dump(self.model_dump(mode="json"), f, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True)
            logger.info("Project '{}' saved successfully to {}.", self.project.name, path)
        except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as e:
            logger.exception("Error saving project '{}'", self.project.name or "<unknown>")
            raise ProjectError from e

    def import_image_files(
        self,
        files: list[Path],
        dest_dir: Path,
        size: SizeType = (512, 512),
        quality: int = 90,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        progress_cb: ProgressCallbackType = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Import specific image files into project storage.

        - Resizes and adjusts quality.
        - Writes to the given destination directory.
        - Raises ImageImportError on failure.
        """
        self._image_ops.import_image_files(
            files=files,
            dest_dir=dest_dir,
            size=size,
            quality=quality,
            overwrite=overwrite,
            progress_cb=progress_cb,
        )

    def import_images(
        self,
        source_path: Path,
        masks_source_path: Path | None = None,
        image_type: ImagesType = ImagesType.RAW,
        size: SizeType = (512, 512),
        quality: int = 90,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        progress_cb: ProgressCallbackType = None,
        split: bool = False,
        train_ratio: float = 0.7,
        val_ratio: float = 0.15,
        test_ratio: float = 0.15,
        random_seed: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Import images (and optional masks) into project storage.

        - Resizes and adjusts quality.
        - Writes to type-specific image/mask destinations.
        - Skips masks if not provided or empty.
        - Raises ImageImportError on failure.
        - If split=True, automatically distributes images across train/val/test splits.
        """
        self._image_ops.import_images(
            source_path=source_path,
            masks_source_path=masks_source_path,
            image_type=image_type,
            size=size,
            quality=quality,
            overwrite=overwrite,
            progress_cb=progress_cb,
            split=split,
            train_ratio=train_ratio,
            val_ratio=val_ratio,
            test_ratio=test_ratio,
            random_seed=random_seed,
        )

    def create_project_dir(self, *, force: bool) -> None:
        """
        Creates the necessary directories for a given project. If the directories already
        exist, it optionally allows overwriting them based on the `force` parameter.

        :param project: The project object containing the `project_path` and `artifacts_path `
        :param force: A boolean indicating whether to forcibly overwrite existing directories
        :return: None
        """
        create_dir(dir_name=self.paths.project_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.paths.artifacts_path, force=force)

        # Create new artifact subdirectories
        create_dir(dir_name=self.models_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.detections_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.detections_visualizations_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.training_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.runtime_path, force=force)

        setup_image_dir(image_path=Path(self.paths.image_path), force=force)
        setup_image_dir(image_path=Path(self.paths.image_mask_path), force=force)

    def clean(self, *, logs_only: bool = False) -> int:
        """Clean temporary files and logs from the project.

        By default, cleans logs, training artifacts, models, and detections.
        Images and masks are always preserved.

        :param logs_only: If True, only clean log files and runtime artifacts,
            preserve models/results
        :return: Number of items removed
        """
        import shutil

        cleaned_count = 0

        # Define paths to clean - always clean runtime directory
        paths_to_clean: list[Path] = [
            self.runtime_path,  # Runtime artifacts (TensorBoard, Lightning logs)
        ]

        # Add log files pattern
        log_dir = Path(self.logging.log_dir)
        if log_dir.exists():
            paths_to_clean.extend(log_dir.glob("*.log"))

        if not logs_only:
            paths_to_clean.extend(
                [
                    self.models_path,  # Model checkpoints
                    self.detections_path,  # Detection results (includes visualizations)
                    self.training_metrics_path,  # Training metrics
                ]
            )

        # Remove paths
        for path in paths_to_clean:
            if path.exists():
                try:
                    if path.is_dir():
                        shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)
                        logger.info("Removed directory: {}", path)
                        cleaned_count += 1
                    else:
                        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                        logger.info("Removed file: {}", path)
                        cleaned_count += 1
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.warning("Failed to remove {}: {}", path, e)

        logger.info("Cleaned {} items from project '{}'", cleaned_count, self.name)
        return cleaned_count

def create_project(
    metadata: ProjectMetadata,
    paths: ProjectPaths,
    ai: AIConfig | None = None,
    logging: LoggingConfig | None = None,
    *,
    force: bool = False,
) -> Project:
    """
    Creates and initializes a new project by defining its attributes, setting up its
    directory structure, and returning the corresponding Project object. It ensures
    proper storage of project-related information including paths and metadata.

    :param paths: necessary paths for the project.
    :param metadata: project metadata.
    :param ai: artificial intelligence configuration.
    :param logging: logging configuration.
    :param force: Boolean flag to force creation, potentially overriding existing data.
    :type force: bool
    :return: The created Project instance containing all initialized attributes.
    :rtype: Project
    """
    # Create fresh copies to avoid shared mutable state issues with pytest-randomly
    if ai is None:
        ai = AIConfig(
            model=default_ai_config.model.model_copy(),
            training=default_ai_config.training.model_copy(),
            detection=default_ai_config.detection.model_copy(),
        )
    if logging is None:
        logging = default_logging_config.model_copy()

    # Set Crackz version on new projects
    if metadata.crackz_version is None:
        from crackz.version import get_version

        metadata.crackz_version = get_version()

    logger.info("Creating new project {}", metadata.name)
    project = Project(
        project=metadata,
        paths=paths,
        ai=ai,
        logging=logging,
    )
    project.create_project_dir(force=force)

    initialize_project_logging(project)

    return project

def load_project(project_file_path: Path) -> Project:
    """
    Loads a project configuration from the specified file path. The
    configuration file is expected to be in YAML format, and its content
    is deserialized into a `Project` object. If the file cannot be opened,
    read, or parsed, the function logs an error.

    Parameters:
        project_file_path (Path): The path to the project configuration file.

    Returns:
        Project | None: The deserialized `Project` object if loading is
        successful. Returns `None` if there is an error during the process.
    """
    try:
        project_file_path = Path(project_file_path)
        with project_file_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
            project = Project(**data)
            logger.info(
                "Project '{}' loaded successfully to {}.",
                project.project.name,
                project_file_path,
            )
            initialize_project_logging(project)
            return project
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}' - not found", project_file_path)
        raise ProjectNotFoundError from e
    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}'", project_file_path)
        raise ProjectConfigError from e
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}'")
        raise ProjectError from e

def load_from_project_path_or_cfg(cfg: Path | None, project_path: Path | None) -> Project:
    """
    Loads a project either from the provided project path or configuration file.

    This function attempts to load a project based on the provided parameters.
    If a project path is provided, the project is loaded from the given path.
    If a configuration file is provided instead, the project is loaded using
    the configuration file. The function prefers the project path if both are
    provided.

    :param cfg: Path to the configuration file for loading the project.
                Can be None if a project path is provided.
    :type cfg: Path | None
    :param project_path: Path to the project directory from which to load
                         the project. Can be None if a configuration file
                         is provided.
    :type project_path: Path | None
    :return: Returns the loaded project instance of type Project.
    :rtype: Project
    """
    if project_path is not None:
        return load_project_from_path(project_path)
    if cfg is not None:
        return load_project(cfg)
    msg = "Either cfg or project_path must be provided."
    logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}'", project_path)
    raise ProjectConfigError(msg)

docs.text:
High‑level detection & training entry points:

AI detection module for crack detection using deep learning models.

This module provides crack detection functionality for harbor infrastructure analysis along with integration of PyTorch Lightning for model training and testing.

Functions: - detect: Detect anomalies using a pre-trained model on the provided project dataset. - train: Train a crack detection model using datasets of a specified project.

Note: This module is a compatibility layer. The actual implementations have been refactored into specialized modules: - detection_runner: Detection logic - training_runner: Training logic - severity: Crack severity categorization - training_setup: Training dataset validation

Datasets:

Dataset classes for crack images.

Dataloaders:

DataLoader utilities for crack images.

Model configuration & LightningModule wrapper:

The core CrackzModel class utilizes a U-Net backbone from segmentation-models-pytorch library for binary segmentation tasks. It computes segmentation logits, applies dice plus focal loss for training, and evaluates performance using the Intersection over Union (IoU) metric. The ComboLoss class implements a weighted combination of Dice and Focal losses for enhanced performance in handling imbalanced datasets.

Callbacks & utilities:

Custom callbacks for PyTorch Lightning.

This module provides callbacks for training and testing progress reporting, metrics collection, and image logging.

The ProgressCallback now includes batch-level progress tracking to provide more accurate time remaining estimates during training. Progress updates are reported every 10 batches (configurable) and at the end of each epoch, ensuring that the GUI and CLI show accurate remaining time even for long epochs with many batches.

Checkpoints:

Model checkpoint management utilities.

Visualization:

Visualization utilities for Crackz AI.

This package contains utilities for plotting, visualization, and graphical output of detection results and metrics.

Device management:

Device management and hardware utilities for Crackz AI.

This package contains utilities for device detection, hardware acceleration, and device-specific operations.

General utilities:

Utility package for Crackz AI - DEPRECATED.

This package has been broken up into more logical top-level packages: - crackz.ai.device: Device management and hardware utilities - crackz.ai.performance: Performance optimization and profiling utilities - crackz.ai.visualization: Plotting and visualization utilities - crackz.ai.pipeline: Workflow orchestration and cancellation support - crackz.ai.compat: Compatibility utilities for different environments - crackz.ai.core: Core types and protocols - crackz.ai.exceptions: AI-related exceptions

Please import directly from these packages instead of using crackz.ai.util.

Examples:

from crackz.ai.device import AIDevice, resolve_device_and_accelerator from crackz.ai.performance import RuntimeTracker, set_global_seed from crackz.ai.core import CrackzBatch, ProgressReporter

Exceptions:

Exceptions related to AI processing and pipeline errors.

This module defines custom exceptions for handling errors within the AI processing pipeline. It includes a hierarchy of exceptions that allow for more nuanced error handling in applications leveraging AI-related functionalities.

def train(  # noqa: C901, PLR0915, PLR0912
    project: Project,
    progress_reporter: ProgressReporter | None = None,
    cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None,
    metrics_callback: MetricsReporter | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Trains a model for crack detection using the provided project data.

    Args:
        project: Loaded project containing configuration and dataset paths.
        progress_reporter: Optional callable for progress updates.
        cancellation_token: Optional token to check for cancellation requests.
        metrics_callback: Optional callable to receive epoch metrics immediately for
            real-time GUI updates.

    Raises:
        CancellationError: If cancellation is requested during training.
    """
    logger.info(f"Training {project.project.name}...")

    reporter = progress_reporter or (lambda _p, _m: None)

    reporter(0.0, "Starting training")

    # Check for cancellation before starting
    if cancellation_token is not None:
        cancellation_token.check_cancelled()

    # Optional reproducibility seed
    if project.ai.training.seed is not None:
        set_global_seed(project.ai.training.seed)
        logger.info("Training seed set to {}", project.ai.training.seed)

    # --- dataset setup ---
    train_ds = CrackzDataset(
        image_dir=project.train_path, image_mask_dir=project.train_mask_path, require_masks=True
    )
    val_ds = CrackzDataset(
        image_dir=project.val_path, image_mask_dir=project.val_mask_path, require_masks=True
    )
    test_ds = CrackzDataset(image_dir=project.test_path, image_mask_dir=project.test_mask_path)

    # Collect warnings about empty datasets
    training_warnings = []
    if len(train_ds) == 0:
        warning_msg = (
            "Training dataset is empty (no valid image-mask pairs found). "
            "All images were skipped because they have no corresponding masks."
        )
        logger.warning(warning_msg)
        training_warnings.append({"type": "empty_train", "message": warning_msg})
    if len(val_ds) == 0:
        warning_msg = (
            "Validation dataset is empty (no valid image-mask pairs found). "
            "All images were skipped because they have no corresponding masks."
        )
        logger.warning(warning_msg)
        training_warnings.append({"type": "empty_val", "message": warning_msg})
    if len(test_ds) == 0:
        warning_msg = (
            "Test dataset is empty (no valid image-mask pairs found). "
            "All images were skipped because they have no corresponding masks."
        )
        logger.warning(warning_msg)
        training_warnings.append({"type": "empty_test", "message": warning_msg})

    # Check if we can proceed with training - need at least train and val datasets
    if len(train_ds) == 0 or len(val_ds) == 0:
        from crackz.ai.exceptions import ImageLoadingError

        # Ensure directory exists before saving warnings
        ensure_dir(project.training_path)

        # Save warnings before failing
        if training_warnings:
            import json

            warnings_path = project.training_path / "training_warnings.json"
            with warnings_path.open("w") as f:
                json.dump(training_warnings, f, indent=2)

        # Raise error with clear message - only mention train/val since test is optional
        empty_sets = []
        if len(train_ds) == 0:
            empty_sets.append("training")
        if len(val_ds) == 0:
            empty_sets.append("validation")

        raise ImageLoadingError(
            f"Cannot proceed with training: {' and '.join(empty_sets)} dataset(s) empty. "
            f"All images were skipped because they have no corresponding masks. "
            f"Add mask files to your images before training."
        )

    # Save warnings to file for display on results page (if training completes)
    if training_warnings:
        import json

        ensure_dir(project.training_path)
        warnings_path = project.training_path / "training_warnings.json"
        with warnings_path.open("w") as f:
            json.dump(training_warnings, f, indent=2)

    # Estimate runtime and create tracker
    device = resolve_device_and_accelerator(project)
    estimated_time = estimate_training_time(
        num_train_images=len(train_ds),
        num_val_images=len(val_ds),
        num_test_images=len(test_ds),
        epochs=project.ai.training.epochs,
        batch_size=project.ai.training.batch_size,
        device=device,
    )
    runtime_tracker = RuntimeTracker(total_time_estimate=estimated_time)
    runtime_tracker.start()

    logger.info(
        "Estimated training time: {} ({} epochs, {} train images, {} val images, {} test images)",
        format_time(estimated_time),
        project.ai.training.epochs,
        len(train_ds),
        len(val_ds),
        len(test_ds),
    )
    reporter(
        0.1,
        f"Datasets ready (estimated time: {format_time(estimated_time)})",
    )

    logger.info(
        "Found {} training images, {} validation images, {} test images",
        len(train_ds),
        len(val_ds),
        len(test_ds),
    )

    train_loader = make_crackz_loader(
        train_ds,
        batch_size=project.ai.training.batch_size,
        shuffle=project.ai.training.shuffle,
        num_workers=project.ai.training.num_workers,
    )
    val_loader = make_crackz_loader(
        val_ds,
        batch_size=project.ai.training.batch_size,
        shuffle=False,
        num_workers=project.ai.training.num_workers,
    )
    test_loader = make_crackz_loader(
        test_ds,
        batch_size=project.ai.training.batch_size,
        shuffle=False,
        num_workers=project.ai.training.num_workers,
    )
    reporter(0.2, "Data loaders ready")

    # --- trainer setup ---
    checkpoint_cb = create_checkpoint_callback(project)
    accelerator = resolve_device_and_accelerator(project)

    metrics_cb = MetricsLoggerCallback(project, reporter=metrics_callback)
    progress_cb = ProgressCallback(
        progress_reporter, runtime_tracker=runtime_tracker, cancellation_token=cancellation_token
    )
    tb_logger = create_tensorboard_logger(project)

    image_logger_cb = None
    if tb_logger and len(val_ds) > 0:
        # Collect a few validation samples (already transformed) for visualization
        sample_tuples: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, str]] = []
        try:
            max_samples = min(4, len(val_ds))
            for idx in range(max_samples):
                sample = val_ds[idx]  # CrackzSample
                sample_tuples.append((sample.image, sample.mask, sample.image_path))
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Failed collecting samples for TensorBoard image logging")
        if sample_tuples:
            image_logger_cb = ImageSampleLogger(sample_tuples)

    callback_list = [
        checkpoint_cb,
        progress_cb,
        metrics_cb,
    ]
    if image_logger_cb:
        callback_list.append(image_logger_cb)

    # Calculate adaptive log interval based on number of training batches
    # Set to 1 if we have few batches, otherwise use 50
    num_train_batches = len(train_loader)
    log_interval = min(50, max(1, num_train_batches))

    trainer = Trainer(
        default_root_dir=str(project.runtime_path),  # Lightning logs go to runtime/
        max_epochs=project.ai.training.epochs,
        accelerator=accelerator,
        logger=tb_logger,
        enable_progress_bar=False,  # disable Lightning's built-in bar
        enable_model_summary=True,
        log_every_n_steps=log_interval,
        num_sanity_val_steps=0,
        callbacks=callback_list,
        **trainer_overrides_from_config(project.ai.training),
    )

    model = CrackzModel(
        config=CrackzConfig.from_project(project, project.ai.training.learning_rate)
    )
    try:
        trainer.fit(model, train_dataloaders=train_loader, val_dataloaders=val_loader)
        trainer.test(model, dataloaders=test_loader)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Training failed.")
        raise

    # --- auto-prune checkpoints if enabled ---
    if getattr(project.ai.training, "auto_prune_checkpoints", False):
        checkpoint_keep = getattr(project.ai.training, "checkpoint_keep", 3)
        try:
            from crackz.ai.model.checkpoints import prune_checkpoints

            removed = prune_checkpoints(project, keep=checkpoint_keep)
            if removed:
                logger.info(
                    "Auto-pruned {} checkpoint(s), keeping top {}",
                    len(removed),
                    checkpoint_keep,
                )
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Auto-pruning checkpoints failed (non-fatal)")

    # --- finalize ---
    logger.info("Training finished. ✅")
    reporter(1.0, "Training finished ✅")

def detect(
    project: Project,
    progress_reporter: ProgressReporter | None = None,
    cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None,
    checkpoint_name: str | None = None,
    result_callback: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    r"""
    Detect cracks in images using a pre-trained model and save annotated results.

    Args:
        project: Loaded project containing configuration, image split paths and model settings.
        progress_reporter: Optional callable receiving (progress: float 0.0-1.0, message: str | None)
            used to report incremental status (CLI/GUI). If None, a no-op reporter is used.
        cancellation_token: Optional token to check for cancellation requests.
        checkpoint_name: Optional checkpoint name to use (e.g., 'best', 'last', 'final', 'epoch-0.9234').
            If None, uses automatic selection (best > last > final).
        result_callback: Optional callable receiving detection results immediately as they're processed.
            Allows GUI to update in real-time without file polling.

    Returns:
        None. Side-effects: writes annotated detection PNGs and a JSON metrics file
        (``detection_results.json``) under the project's detections path.

    Raises:
        CancellationError: If cancellation is requested during detection.
    """  # noqa: E501
    reporter: ProgressReporter = (
        progress_reporter if progress_reporter is not None else _noop_reporter
    )
    reporter(0.0, "Starting detection")

    # Check for cancellation before starting
    if cancellation_token is not None:
        cancellation_token.check_cancelled()

    # Ensure a trained model is available before detection
    if not has_trained_model(project):
        reporter(1.0, "No trained model found. Detection skipped. ❌")
        logger.warning("Detection skipped: no trained model found.")
        return

    # Setup
    device, model, loader, runtime_tracker, total_images = _setup_detection(
        project, reporter, checkpoint_name
    )

    # Use visualizations subdirectory for PNG files
    visualizations_dir = project.detections_visualizations_path
    ensure_dir(visualizations_dir)

    # Main detections directory for JSON results
    detections_dir = project.detections_path
    ensure_dir(detections_dir)

    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    threshold = project.ai.model.threshold
    batch_size = project.ai.detection.batch_size

    # Inference loop
    for batch_idx, batch in enumerate(loader):
        # Check for cancellation before processing each batch
        if cancellation_token is not None:
            cancellation_token.check_cancelled()

        _process_detection_batch(
            batch_idx,
            batch,
            model,
            device,
            threshold,
            visualizations_dir,  # PNG files go to visualizations/
            detections_dir,  # JSON file goes to detections/
            results,
            reporter,
            runtime_tracker,
            total_images,
            batch_size,
            save_interval=5,  # Save every 5 images to balance responsiveness and performance
            result_callback=result_callback,  # Pass callback for real-time GUI updates
        )

    # Finalize
    save_metrics_json(results=results, output_dir=detections_dir)
    reporter(1.0, "Detection finished ✅")

    """Categorize crack detection severity based on confidence level.

    Args:
        confidence: Mean prediction probability (0.0 to 1.0)

    Returns:
        Severity category: "Crack Detected", "Probable Crack", or "Possible Crack"

class CrackzDataset(Dataset[Sample]):
    """Dataset for crack images with optional masks."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        image_dir: Path | str,
        image_mask_dir: Path | str,
        transform: ImageTransform | None = None,
        mask_transform: MaskTransform | None = None,
        normalization_config: NormalizationConfig | None = None,
        *,
        require_masks: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        self.image_dir = Path(image_dir).resolve()
        self.image_mask_dir = Path(image_mask_dir).resolve()
        self.require_masks = require_masks

        all_files = sorted(
            [
                p
                for p in self.image_dir.glob("*")
                if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in SUPPORTED_IMAGE_EXTS
            ]
        )

        # Filter out images without masks if masks are required
        if require_masks:
            self.files = []
            skipped = 0
            for img_path in all_files:
                # Look for PNG mask only
                mask_path = self.image_mask_dir / f"{img_path.stem}.png"

                if mask_path.exists():
                    self.files.append(img_path)
                else:
                    skipped += 1
                    logger.debug("Skipping {} - no mask found", img_path.stem)

            if skipped > 0:
                logger.info(
                    "Skipped {} image(s) without masks (require_masks=True). "
                    "Using {} images with masks.",
                    skipped,
                    len(self.files),
                )
        else:
            self.files = all_files

        # Only raise an error if the directory is truly empty (no images at all)
        # If images were found but filtered out due to missing masks, that's valid (length 0)
        if not self.files and not all_files:
            # Gather a brief diagnostic of what's in the directory to aid users.
            existing = [p.name for p in self.image_dir.glob("*") if p.is_file()][:10]
            hint_parts = [
                (
                    f"No images found in {self.image_dir}. Supported extensions: "
                    f"{sorted(SUPPORTED_IMAGE_EXTS)}."
                ),
                "If your files use another extension or live under 'raw', "
                "import them with --type train",
                "or move/symlink them into the expected split directory.",
            ]
            hint = " ".join(hint_parts)
            if existing:
                hint += f" Found non-matching files: {existing}."
            raise ImageLoadingError(hint)

        mean = normalization_config.mean if normalization_config else [0.485, 0.456, 0.406]
        std = normalization_config.std if normalization_config else [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]

        self.transform = transform or transforms.Compose(
            [
                ToRGB(),
                transforms.ToTensor(),
                transforms.Normalize(mean=mean, std=std),
            ]
        )
        self.mask_transform = mask_transform or transforms.Compose([transforms.ToTensor()])

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.files)

    def __getitem__(self, idx: int) -> Sample:
        img_path = self.files[idx]

        # Use CrackzImage for consistent image loading and error handling
        try:
            img = load_image_with_crackz_image(img_path)
            x = self.transform(img)
        except ImageLoadingError:
            # Re-raise ImageLoadingError as-is for proper error handling
            raise
        except Exception as e:
            # Wrap unexpected errors in ImageLoadingError
            raise ImageLoadingError(f"Failed to process image {img_path}: {e}") from e

        _, h, w = x.shape

        # Look for PNG mask only
        mask_path = self.image_mask_dir / f"{img_path.stem}.png"

        if mask_path.exists():
            # Use CrackzImage for mask loading as well for consistency
            try:
                mask_crackz_img = CrackzImage(path=mask_path)
                mask_img = mask_crackz_img.image.convert("L")
                y = self.mask_transform(mask_img)
                # Binarize mask: any non-zero value becomes 1
                y = (y > 0).float()
            except (ImageFileError, Exception) as e:
                raise ImageLoadingError(f"Failed to load mask {mask_path}: {e}") from e
        else:
            # If masks are required, this should never happen due to filtering in __init__
            # If masks are not required (detection mode), use dummy mask
            if self.require_masks:
                raise ImageLoadingError(
                    f"Mask required but not found for {img_path.stem}.png. "
                    "This should not happen - check dataset initialization."
                )
            # Don't log in detection mode - dummy masks are expected
            y = torch.zeros((1, h, w), dtype=torch.float32)

        return CrackzSample(x, y, str(img_path))

def load_image_with_crackz_image(image_path: Path) -> PILImage.Image:
    """Load an image using CrackzImage for consistent error handling and file management.

    This function provides a standardized way to load images across the AI pipeline,
    ensuring consistent error handling and proper file handle management.

    Args:
        image_path: Path to the image file

    Returns:
        PIL Image object

    Raises:

    try:

    except Exception as e:

    image_dir: Path | str,
    transform: ImageTransform | None = None,
    normalization_config: NormalizationConfig | None = None,

    Args:
        image_dir: Directory containing images to process
        transform: Optional image transformations

    return CrackzDataset(

        image_mask_dir=dummy_mask_dir,
        transform=transform,
        mask_transform=None,
        normalization_config=normalization_config,
        require_masks=False,
    )

def create_training_datasets(
    train_path: Path,
    train_mask_path: Path,
    val_path: Path,
    val_mask_path: Path,
    test_path: Path,
    test_mask_path: Path,
) -> tuple[CrackzDataset, CrackzDataset, CrackzDataset]:
    """Create training, validation, and test datasets.

    Args:
        train_path: Path to training images directory
        train_mask_path: Path to training masks directory
        val_path: Path to validation images directory
        val_mask_path: Path to validation masks directory
        test_path: Path to test images directory
        test_mask_path: Path to test masks directory

    Returns:
        Tuple of (train_ds, val_ds, test_ds)

    Note:
        Images without corresponding masks will be skipped with a warning logged.
        Empty datasets are allowed - PyTorch will raise an error later if needed.
    """
    train_ds = CrackzDataset(
        image_dir=train_path, image_mask_dir=train_mask_path, require_masks=True
    )
    val_ds = CrackzDataset(image_dir=val_path, image_mask_dir=val_mask_path, require_masks=True)
    test_ds = CrackzDataset(image_dir=test_path, image_mask_dir=test_mask_path, require_masks=True)

    # Just log warnings for empty datasets, don't raise exceptions
    if len(train_ds) == 0:
        logger.warning("Training dataset is empty (no valid image-mask pairs in {})", train_path)
    if len(val_ds) == 0:
        logger.warning("Validation dataset is empty (no valid image-mask pairs in {})", val_path)
    if len(test_ds) == 0:
        logger.warning("Test dataset is empty (no valid image-mask pairs in {})", test_path)

    return train_ds, val_ds, test_ds

def collate(batch: list[CrackzSample]) -> CrackzBatch:
    """Collate samples into a batch.

    Handles both training samples (CrackzSample with real masks) and detection samples
    (CrackzSample with dummy masks). Detection samples have dummy zero masks that are ignored.
    """
    # All batches are now CrackzSample format (unified interface)
    shapes = [s.image.shape for s in batch]
    if len(set(shapes)) > 1:
        logger.warning(f"Image size mismatch in batch: {shapes}")

    images = torch.stack([s.image for s in batch], 0)  # [B,C,H,W]
    masks = torch.stack([s.mask for s in batch], 0)  # [B,1,H,W]
    paths = [s.image_path for s in batch]
    return CrackzBatch(images=images, masks=masks, paths=paths)

    train_ds: CrackzDataset,
    val_ds: CrackzDataset,
    test_ds: CrackzDataset,
    batch_size: int,
    num_workers: int,

    Args:
        train_ds: Training dataset
        val_ds: Validation dataset

    test_loader = make_crackz_loader(
        test_ds,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=False,

    return train_loader, val_loader, test_loader

class ComboLoss(torch.nn.Module):
    """Combination of Dice Loss and Focal Loss for binary segmentation."""

    def __init__(self, dice_weight: float = 1.0, focal_weight: float = 1.0) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.dice = smp.losses.DiceLoss(mode="binary")
        self.focal = smp.losses.FocalLoss(mode="binary")
        self.dice_weight = dice_weight
        self.focal_weight = focal_weight

    def forward(self, y_pred: Tensor, y_true: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """
        Computes the combined loss using a weighted sum of Dice loss and Focal loss.

        This method calculates the weighted combination of Dice loss and Focal loss
        based on the specified coefficients. It is typically used in segmentation
        tasks to improve detection of foreground classes by balancing loss
        contributions and handling class imbalances effectively.

        :param y_pred: Predicted tensor values.
        :param y_true: Ground truth tensor values.
        :return: Combined loss value as a tensor.
        """
        dice_loss: Tensor = cast("Tensor", self.dice(y_pred, y_true))

        # MPS compatibility fix for focal loss
        # The focal loss in smp uses .type() which doesn't work with MPS tensors
        # Compute on CPU and move result back to original device
        if y_pred.device.type == "mps":
            device = y_pred.device
            y_pred_cpu = y_pred.cpu()
            y_true_cpu = y_true.cpu()
            focal_loss_cpu: Tensor = cast("Tensor", self.focal(y_pred_cpu, y_true_cpu))
            focal_loss = focal_loss_cpu.to(device)
        else:
            focal_loss = cast("Tensor", self.focal(y_pred, y_true))

        total: Tensor = self.dice_weight * dice_loss + self.focal_weight * focal_loss
        return total

class CrackzModel(l.LightningModule):
    """PyTorch Lightning module for crack segmentation."""

    def __init__(self, config: CrackzConfig) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.save_hyperparameters()
        self.lr = config.lr

        self.model = smp.Unet(
            encoder_name=config.encoder,
            encoder_weights=config.encoder_weights,
            in_channels=config.in_channels,
            classes=config.num_classes,
        )

        self.criterion: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor] = self.get_loss_function(config)

        self.train_iou = BinaryJaccardIndex(threshold=config.threshold)
        self.val_iou = BinaryJaccardIndex(threshold=config.threshold)
        self.test_iou = BinaryJaccardIndex(threshold=config.threshold)

        # Add accuracy metrics
        from torchmetrics.classification import BinaryAccuracy

        self.train_acc = BinaryAccuracy(threshold=config.threshold)
        self.val_acc = BinaryAccuracy(threshold=config.threshold)
        self.test_acc = BinaryAccuracy(threshold=config.threshold)

        self.threshold = config.threshold

    def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:  # noqa: D102
        return self.model(x)

    def _shared_step(self, batch: CrackzBatch, stage: str) -> Tensor:
        b = self._extract_batch(batch)  # normalize to CrackzBatch
        x, y, _ = b.images, b.masks, b.paths
        batch_size = x.shape[0] if hasattr(x, "shape") else None

        preds = self(x)  # logits
        loss = self.criterion(preds, y)

        # probabilities for metric
        probs = torch.sigmoid(preds)

        if stage == "train":
            iou = self.train_iou(probs, y)
            acc = self.train_acc(probs, y)
        elif stage == "val":
            iou = self.val_iou(probs, y)
            acc = self.val_acc(probs, y)
        else:
            iou = self.test_iou(probs, y)
            acc = self.test_acc(probs, y)

        self.log(
            f"{stage}_loss",
            loss,
            on_step=(stage == "train"),
            on_epoch=True,
            prog_bar=True,
            batch_size=batch_size,
        )
        self.log(
            f"{stage}_iou",
            iou,
            on_step=False,
            on_epoch=True,
            prog_bar=True,
            batch_size=batch_size,
        )
        self.log(
            f"{stage}_acc",
            acc,
            on_step=False,
            on_epoch=True,
            prog_bar=True,
            batch_size=batch_size,
        )

        return loss

    def training_step(self, batch: CrackzBatch, _batch_idx: int) -> Tensor:
        """Perform a training step."""
        return self._shared_step(batch, "train")

    def validation_step(self, batch: CrackzBatch, _batch_idx: int) -> None:
        """Validate a step."""
        self._shared_step(batch, "val")

    def test_step(self, batch: CrackzBatch, _batch_idx: int) -> None:  # noqa: PT019
        """Perform a test step."""
        self._shared_step(batch, "test")

    def on_train_epoch_end(self) -> None:
        """Reset training metrics at epoch end."""
        self.train_iou.reset()
        self.train_acc.reset()

    def on_validation_epoch_end(self) -> None:
        """Reset validation metrics at epoch end."""
        self.val_iou.reset()
        self.val_acc.reset()

    def on_test_epoch_end(self) -> None:
        """Reset test metrics at epoch end."""
        self.test_iou.reset()
        self.test_acc.reset()

    def configure_optimizers(self) -> Optimizer:
        """Configure the AdamW optimizer."""
        return AdamW(self.parameters(), lr=self.lr)

    def get_loss_function(self, config: CrackzConfig) -> ComboLoss | DiceLoss:
        """Get the loss function based on the configuration."""
        if not config.loss_name or config.loss_name.lower() == "combo":
            return ComboLoss(dice_weight=config.dice_weight, focal_weight=config.focal_weight)
        logger.warning("Loss name not recognized, using Dice Loss.")
        return smp.losses.DiceLoss(mode="binary")

    def _extract_batch(self, batch: CrackzBatch | Batch | tuple | list) -> CrackzBatch:
        """
        Normalize various batch types into a CrackzBatch.

        Args:
            batch (CrackzBatch | Batch | tuple | list): A batch provided by the DataLoader
                or something that matches the Batch protocol.

        Returns:
            CrackzBatch: A normalized batch with images, masks, and optional paths.
        """
        # Case 0: Already a CrackzBatch
        if isinstance(batch, CrackzBatch):
            return batch

        # Case 1: tuple/list from DataLoader (x, y, [paths])
        if isinstance(batch, (tuple, list)):
            if len(batch) == 3:  # (images, masks, paths)  # noqa: PLR2004
                x, y, paths = batch
            elif len(batch) == 2:  # (images, masks)  # noqa: PLR2004
                x, y = batch
                paths = None
            else:
                raise DataLoadingError(f"Unexpected batch length {len(batch)}: {batch}")
            return CrackzBatch(images=x, masks=y, paths=paths)

        # Case 2: Already matches Batch protocol
        if hasattr(batch, "images") and hasattr(batch, "masks"):
            return CrackzBatch(
                images=batch.images,
                masks=batch.masks,
                paths=getattr(batch, "paths", None),
            )

        raise TypeError(f"Unsupported batch type: {type(batch)}")

class MetricsLoggerCallback(pl.Callback):
    """Collects and persists scalar metrics; optionally forwards them to an external reporter."""

    def __init__(self, project: Project, reporter: MetricsReporter | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.project = project
        self._reporter = reporter
        self.history: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
        self.output_dir: Path = project.training_path  # unchanged
        self.train_metrics: list[dict] = []
        self.val_metrics: list[dict] = []
        self.test_metrics: list[dict] = []
        self._total_epochs: int | None = None

    def on_train_start(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Store total epochs when training starts."""
        self._total_epochs = trainer.max_epochs

    def on_train_batch_end(
        self,
        trainer: pl.Trainer,
        pl_module: pl.LightningModule,  # noqa: ARG002
        outputs,  # noqa: ANN001, ARG002
        batch,  # noqa: ANN001, ARG002
        batch_idx,  # noqa: ANN001
    ) -> None:
        """Update running metrics for live GUI updates during long epochs.

        Writes current metrics to training_metrics.json every 10 batches.
        The main metrics history is preserved and only updated at epoch end.
        """
        # Only update every 10 batches to avoid excessive I/O
        if batch_idx % 10 == 0:
            # Get current logged metrics (running averages during epoch)
            current_metrics = trainer.logged_metrics
            snapshot: dict[str, float] = {}
            for k, v in current_metrics.items():
                f = self._to_float(v)
                if f is not None and not k.lower().endswith("_step"):
                    snapshot[k] = f

            if snapshot:
                # Add current running metrics as a temporary epoch entry
                # This will be replaced when the epoch actually completes
                temp_epoch = {
                    "epoch": trainer.current_epoch,
                    "batch": batch_idx,
                    "partial": True,  # Flag to indicate this is mid-epoch data
                    **snapshot,
                }

                # Save with temporary running data
                # The train_metrics list will be updated with final values at epoch end
                self._save_with_running_data(temp_epoch)

    def on_train_epoch_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Capture training metrics at the end of each training epoch."""
        self._capture(trainer.callback_metrics, phase="train", epoch=trainer.current_epoch)

    def on_validation_epoch_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Capture validation metrics at the end of validation."""
        self._capture(trainer.callback_metrics, phase="val", epoch=trainer.current_epoch)

    def on_test_epoch_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Capture test metrics at the end of testing."""
        self._capture(
            trainer.callback_metrics, phase="test", epoch=getattr(trainer, "current_epoch", None)
        )

    def on_fit_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Final save at the end of training."""
        self._save()

    def _to_float(self, v: Any) -> float | None:  # noqa: ANN401
        if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor):
            if v.numel() == 1:
                return float(v.detach().cpu().item())
            return None
        if isinstance(v, Number):
            # Convert Number to float - works for int, float, complex.real, etc.
            try:
                return float(v)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                return None
        return None

    def _capture(self, metrics: dict[str, Any], phase: str, epoch: int | None) -> None:  # noqa: C901
        snapshot: dict[str, float] = {}
        global_step = None
        for k, v in metrics.items():
            # Capture global_step separately
            if k.lower() == "global_step":
                f = self._to_float(v)
                if f is not None:
                    global_step = int(f)
                continue

            f = self._to_float(v)
            if f is not None and not k.lower().endswith("_step"):
                self.history.setdefault(k, []).append(f)
                snapshot[k] = f
        if not snapshot:
            return
        if self._reporter:
            self._reporter({"phase": phase, **snapshot})  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        record = {"epoch": epoch, **snapshot}
        if global_step is not None:
            record["global_step"] = global_step
        if phase == "train":
            self.train_metrics.append(record)
        elif phase == "val":
            self.val_metrics.append(record)
        elif phase == "test":
            self.test_metrics.append(record)
        self._save()

    def _save(self) -> None:
        self.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Merge training and validation metrics by epoch for the epochs list
        # This ensures the GUI shows complete data immediately after each epoch
        merged_epochs = self._merge_train_val_epochs()

        payload = {
            "train": self.train_metrics,
            "val": self.val_metrics,
            "epochs": merged_epochs,  # Use merged data for GUI display
            "total_epochs": self._total_epochs,
            "test": self.test_metrics,
            "updated_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00", "Z"),
        }
        path = self.output_dir / "training_metrics.json"
        try:
            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(payload, f, indent=2)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("failed to write metrics JSON: {}", e)

    def _merge_train_val_epochs(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Merge training and validation metrics by epoch number.

        Returns a list where each entry contains both train and val metrics
        for that epoch, providing a complete view for GUI display.
        """
        merged: dict[int, dict] = {}

        # Add training metrics
        for entry in self.train_metrics:
            epoch = entry.get("epoch")
            if epoch is not None:
                merged[epoch] = {"epoch": epoch}
                for k, v in entry.items():
                    if k != "epoch":
                        merged[epoch][k] = v

        # Add validation metrics
        for entry in self.val_metrics:
            epoch = entry.get("epoch")
            if epoch is not None:
                if epoch not in merged:
                    merged[epoch] = {"epoch": epoch}
                for k, v in entry.items():
                    if k != "epoch":
                        merged[epoch][k] = v

        # Return sorted by epoch number
        return [merged[epoch] for epoch in sorted(merged.keys())]

    def _save_with_running_data(self, running_epoch: dict) -> None:
        """Save metrics including current running epoch data for live GUI updates.

        This temporarily adds the running epoch to the epochs list so the GUI
        can display progress during long epochs. The running data is marked with
        'partial': True and will be replaced with final metrics at epoch end.
        """
        self.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # Start with merged train/val epochs
        epochs_with_running = self._merge_train_val_epochs()

        # Remove any existing partial entry for this epoch
        epochs_with_running = [e for e in epochs_with_running if not e.get("partial", False)]

        # Add the running epoch data
        epochs_with_running.append(running_epoch)

        payload = {
            "epochs": epochs_with_running,
            "total_epochs": self._total_epochs,
            "train": self.train_metrics,
            "val": self.val_metrics,
            "test": self.test_metrics,
            "updated_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds").replace("+00:00", "Z"),
        }
        path = self.output_dir / "training_metrics.json"
        try:
            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(payload, f, indent=2)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("failed to write metrics JSON: {}", e)
