Bases: Callback

Reports training/testing progress via an optional external reporter.

This callback tracks progress at both the epoch and batch level to provide accurate time remaining estimates. Progress updates are reported: - At the start and end of each training epoch - Every 10 batches during training (configurable via update_interval) - At the end of each epoch (always) - At the end of training and testing

The batch-level progress tracking ensures that long epochs with many batches show continuously updating progress and accurate time estimates, which is especially important for GUI displays.

Source code in src/crackz/ai/training/callbacks.py 
class ProgressCallback(pl.Callback):
    """Reports training/testing progress via an optional external reporter.

    This callback tracks progress at both the epoch and batch level to provide
    accurate time remaining estimates. Progress updates are reported:
    - At the start and end of each training epoch
    - Every 10 batches during training (configurable via update_interval)
    - At the end of each epoch (always)
    - At the end of training and testing

    The batch-level progress tracking ensures that long epochs with many batches
    show continuously updating progress and accurate time estimates, which is
    especially important for GUI displays.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        reporter: ProgressReporter | None = None,
        runtime_tracker: RuntimeTracker | None = None,
        cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._reporter = reporter
        self._runtime_tracker = runtime_tracker
        self._cancellation_token = cancellation_token
        self._total_train_batches: int | None = None
        self._batches_processed: int = 0

    def __call__(self, progress: float, message: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Report progress via the reporter or log it."""
        # Enhance message with time information if tracker is available
        if self._runtime_tracker is not None:
            message = self._runtime_tracker.format_status(progress, message)

        if self._reporter:
            self._reporter(progress, message)
        else:
            logger.info("progress %.2f %s", progress, message or "")

    # PL hooks
    def on_train_start(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Calculate total batches for progress tracking."""
        # Get total number of batches per epoch from the trainer
        if trainer.num_training_batches > 0:
            self._total_train_batches = trainer.num_training_batches * trainer.max_epochs
        self._batches_processed = 0

    def on_train_epoch_start(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Report progress at the start of each training epoch."""
        # Check for cancellation
        if self._cancellation_token is not None:
            self._cancellation_token.check_cancelled()

        frac = trainer.current_epoch / max(1, trainer.max_epochs)
        self(0.2 + frac * 0.7, f"epoch {trainer.current_epoch + 1}/{trainer.max_epochs} started")

    def on_train_batch_end(
        self,
        trainer: pl.Trainer,
        pl_module: pl.LightningModule,  # noqa: ARG002
        outputs: Any,  # noqa: ANN401, ARG002
        batch: Any,  # noqa: ANN401, ARG002
        batch_idx: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Report progress after each training batch for more accurate time estimates."""
        self._batches_processed += 1

        # Only update progress every N batches to avoid overhead
        # Update every 10 batches or on the last batch of the epoch
        update_interval = 10
        is_last_batch = batch_idx == trainer.num_training_batches - 1

        if (
            (self._batches_processed % update_interval == 0 or is_last_batch)
            and self._total_train_batches
            and self._total_train_batches > 0
        ):
            # Calculate fine-grained progress based on batches
            batch_frac = self._batches_processed / self._total_train_batches
            # Map to the training portion of overall progress (0.2 to 0.9)
            progress = 0.2 + batch_frac * 0.7

            # Create a detailed status message
            epoch_num = trainer.current_epoch + 1
            batch_in_epoch = batch_idx + 1
            total_batches_in_epoch = trainer.num_training_batches
            message = (
                f"epoch {epoch_num}/{trainer.max_epochs} "
                f"batch {batch_in_epoch}/{total_batches_in_epoch}"
            )

            self(progress, message)

    def on_train_epoch_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Report progress at the end of each training epoch."""
        # Check for cancellation
        if self._cancellation_token is not None:
            self._cancellation_token.check_cancelled()

        frac = (trainer.current_epoch + 1) / max(1, trainer.max_epochs)
        self(0.2 + frac * 0.7, f"epoch {trainer.current_epoch + 1} finished")

    def on_fit_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Report progress at the end of training."""
        self(0.95, "training finished; testing...")

    def on_test_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """Report progress at the end of testing."""
        self(1.0, "✅ training + testing complete")

) -> None:
    """Report progress after each training batch for more accurate time estimates."""
    self._batches_processed += 1

    # Only update progress every N batches to avoid overhead
    # Update every 10 batches or on the last batch of the epoch
    update_interval = 10
    is_last_batch = batch_idx == trainer.num_training_batches - 1

    if (
        (self._batches_processed % update_interval == 0 or is_last_batch)
        and self._total_train_batches
        and self._total_train_batches > 0
    ):
        # Calculate fine-grained progress based on batches
        batch_frac = self._batches_processed / self._total_train_batches
        # Map to the training portion of overall progress (0.2 to 0.9)
        progress = 0.2 + batch_frac * 0.7

        # Create a detailed status message
        epoch_num = trainer.current_epoch + 1
        batch_in_epoch = batch_idx + 1
        total_batches_in_epoch = trainer.num_training_batches
        message = (
            f"epoch {epoch_num}/{trainer.max_epochs} "
            f"batch {batch_in_epoch}/{total_batches_in_epoch}"
        )

        self(progress, message)

Logs sample input / prediction / mask triplets to TensorBoard after validation epochs.

This callback is added only when a TensorBoard logger is active. It keeps a small, fixed set of samples (to avoid touching the dataloaders again) and performs a forward pass in eval/no_grad context to obtain predictions. Images are denormalized using the standard ImageNet statistics (same as dataset defaults) before logging.

Source code in src/crackz/ai/training/callbacks.py 
class ImageSampleLogger(pl.Callback):
    """Logs sample input / prediction / mask triplets to TensorBoard after validation epochs.

    This callback is added only when a TensorBoard logger is active. It keeps a small, fixed
    set of samples (to avoid touching the dataloaders again) and performs a forward pass
    in eval/no_grad context to obtain predictions. Images are denormalized using the
    standard ImageNet statistics (same as dataset defaults) before logging.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        samples: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, str]],
        *,
        max_images: int = 4,
        mean: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.485, 0.456, 0.406),
        std: tuple[float, float, float] = (0.229, 0.224, 0.225),
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.samples = samples[:max_images]
        self.mean = torch.tensor(mean).view(3, 1, 1)
        self.std = torch.tensor(std).view(3, 1, 1)

    def _denorm(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x: [C,H,W] normalized -> clamp to 0..1 after denorm
        return (x * self.std + self.mean).clamp(0, 1)

    def on_validation_epoch_end(self, trainer: pl.Trainer, pl_module: pl.LightningModule) -> None:
        """Log a grid of sample input / ground-truth / prediction images to TensorBoard.

        Executed after each validation epoch when a TensorBoard logger is present.
        Skips silently if no samples or logger are available.
        """
        if not trainer.logger or not hasattr(trainer.logger, "experiment"):
            return
        if not self.samples:
            return

        logger.debug("Logging sample images to TensorBoard")
        device = pl_module.device
        pl_module.eval()
        grids: list[torch.Tensor] = []

        with torch.no_grad():
            rows: list[torch.Tensor] = []
            for img_t, mask_t, _path in self.samples:  # renamed unused variable
                img = img_t.to(device)
                mask = mask_t.to(device)
                pred_logits = pl_module(img.unsqueeze(0))  # [1,1,H,W]
                pred_prob = torch.sigmoid(pred_logits)[0, 0]
                pred_bin = (pred_prob > pl_module.threshold).float()

                # Build 3-panel row: input, gt mask, pred mask
                img_vis = self._denorm(img.cpu())  # [3,H,W]
                gt_vis = mask.cpu().repeat(3, 1, 1)  # replicate to 3 channels
                pr_vis = pred_bin.cpu().repeat(3, 1, 1)
                row = torch.stack([img_vis, gt_vis, pr_vis], 0)  # [3,3,H,W]
                # flatten into grid row (concatenate horizontally)
                row_grid = make_grid(row, nrow=3)  # [3,H, 3W]
                rows.append(row_grid)

            # Stack rows vertically by concatenating along height -> make_grid again
            # Add small separator (optional)
            grid = torch.cat(rows, dim=1)  # [3, totalH, 3W]
            grids.append(grid)

        global_step = trainer.global_step
        # Type checker doesn't know logger has experiment after hasattr check
        trainer.logger.experiment.add_image(
            "samples/input_gt_pred",
            grids[0],
            global_step=global_step,
        )

def create_training_callbacks(
    project: Project,
    val_ds: CrackzDataset,
    tb_logger: TensorBoardLogger | None,
    progress_reporter: ProgressReporter | None,
    runtime_tracker: RuntimeTracker,
    cancellation_token: CancellationToken | None,
) -> list[Any]:
    """Create callbacks for training including checkpoint, metrics, progress, and image logging.

    Args:
        project: Project configuration
        val_ds: Validation dataset for sampling images
        tb_logger: TensorBoard logger instance or None if disabled
        progress_reporter: Optional progress reporter callback
        runtime_tracker: Runtime tracker for time estimation
        cancellation_token: Optional cancellation token

    Returns:
        List of PyTorch Lightning callbacks
    """
    # Import here to avoid circular dependency
    from crackz.ai.checkpoints import create_checkpoint_callback

    checkpoint_cb = create_checkpoint_callback(project)
    metrics_cb = MetricsLoggerCallback(project)
    progress_cb = ProgressCallback(
        progress_reporter, runtime_tracker=runtime_tracker, cancellation_token=cancellation_token
    )

    callback_list: list[Any] = [
        checkpoint_cb,
        progress_cb,
        metrics_cb,
    ]

    # Add image logger if TensorBoard is enabled and validation data exists
    if tb_logger and len(val_ds) > 0:
        sample_tuples: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, str]] = []
        try:
            max_samples = min(4, len(val_ds))
            for idx in range(max_samples):
                sample = val_ds[idx]  # CrackzSample
                sample_tuples.append((sample.image, sample.mask, sample.image_path))
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Failed collecting samples for TensorBoard image logging")
        if sample_tuples:
            image_logger_cb = ImageSampleLogger(sample_tuples)
            callback_list.append(image_logger_cb)

    return callback_list

def get_available_checkpoints(checkpoints_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """
    Get all available checkpoint files in the directory.

    Args:
        checkpoints_dir: Directory containing checkpoint files

    Returns:
        List of checkpoint paths sorted by priority (best, final, last, then others by name)
    """
    if not checkpoints_dir.exists():
        return []

    all_ckpts = list(checkpoints_dir.glob("*.ckpt"))

    # Sort by priority: best > final > last > others (alphabetically)
    def priority_key(ckpt: Path) -> tuple[int, str]:
        name = ckpt.name
        if name == BEST_CKPT_NAME:
            return (0, name)
        if name == FINAL_CKPT_NAME:
            return (1, name)
        if name == LAST_CKPT_NAME:
            return (2, name)
        return (3, name)

    return sorted(all_ckpts, key=priority_key)

def select_checkpoint(checkpoints_dir: Path) -> Path | None:
    """
    Select the best available checkpoint file in order of preference:
    1) best.ckpt
    2) last.ckpt
    3) final.ckpt.

    Args:
        checkpoints_dir: Directory containing checkpoint files

    Returns:
        Path to selected checkpoint or None if none found
    """
    best = checkpoints_dir / BEST_CKPT_NAME
    last = checkpoints_dir / LAST_CKPT_NAME
    final = checkpoints_dir / FINAL_CKPT_NAME

    if best.exists():
        logger.debug("Selected checkpoint: {} (best)", best)
        return best
    if last.exists():
        logger.debug("Selected checkpoint: {} (last)", last)
        return last
    if final.exists():
        logger.debug("Selected checkpoint: {} (final)", final)
        return final

    logger.error(
        "No checkpoint files found in {} (tried: {}, {}, {})",
        checkpoints_dir,
        best,
        last,
        final,
    )
    return None

def load_model_from_checkpoint(
    project: Project, lr: float, checkpoint_name: str | None = None
) -> CrackzModel:
    """Load a CrackzModel from the project's checkpoint directory.

    Args:
        project: Project configuration
        lr: Learning rate for the model
        checkpoint_name: Optional checkpoint name (e.g., 'best', 'last', 'epoch-0.9234').
            If None, uses automatic selection (best > last > final).
            Can be specified with or without the '.ckpt' extension.

    Returns:
        Loaded model or new untrained model if no checkpoint found
    """
    from crackz.ai.model import CrackzConfig, CrackzModel

    # If checkpoint_name is specified, use it directly
    if checkpoint_name is not None:
        # Add .ckpt extension if not present
        if not checkpoint_name.endswith(".ckpt"):
            checkpoint_name = f"{checkpoint_name}.ckpt"

        checkpoint_path = project.checkpoints_path / checkpoint_name

        if not checkpoint_path.exists():
            logger.error(
                "Specified checkpoint {} not found in {}",
                checkpoint_name,
                project.checkpoints_path,
            )
            raise ModelNotFoundError(f"Checkpoint not found: {checkpoint_path}")

        loader = CrackzModel.load_from_checkpoint
        model = loader(checkpoint_path)
        logger.info("✅ Model loaded from checkpoint {}", checkpoint_path)
        return model

    # Use automatic selection
    selected_ckpt: Path | None = select_checkpoint(project.checkpoints_path)

    if not selected_ckpt or not selected_ckpt.exists():
        logger.warning(
            "No checkpoint found in {} returning untrained model.", project.checkpoints_path
        )
        return CrackzModel(CrackzConfig.from_project(project, lr))

    loader = CrackzModel.load_from_checkpoint
    model = loader(selected_ckpt)
    logger.info("✅ Model loaded from checkpoint {}", selected_ckpt)
    return model

def create_checkpoint_callback(project: Project) -> ModelCheckpoint:
    """
    Create a ModelCheckpoint callback configured to save the best model (by val_iou)
    and the last checkpoint into the project's checkpoints directory.

    Uses project.ai.training.save_top_k and save_last configuration.

    Args:
        project: Project configuration

    Returns:
        Configured ModelCheckpoint callback
    """
    from crackz.util import ensure_dir

    checkpoints_dir = project.checkpoints_path
    ensure_dir(checkpoints_dir)

    # Use configuration values with backwards-compatible defaults
    save_top_k = getattr(project.ai.training, "save_top_k", 1)
    save_last = getattr(project.ai.training, "save_last", True)

    callback = ModelCheckpoint(
        dirpath=checkpoints_dir,
        filename=CKPT_FILENAME_PATTERN,
        save_top_k=save_top_k,
        monitor="val_iou",
        mode="max",
        save_last=save_last,
        # Add async saving to reduce memory pressure
        enable_version_counter=False,
    )
    # Make dirpath a Path object to keep consistency across our codebase and tests
    callback.dirpath = checkpoints_dir
    return callback

def prune_checkpoints(project: Project, keep: int) -> list[Path]:
    """Prune older checkpoints, keeping only the top N based on a scoring heuristic.

    Scoring heuristic:
    - best.ckpt: score 2.0 (highest priority)
    - final.ckpt: score 1.5
    - last.ckpt: score 0.5
    - Other checkpoints: score 0.0 (lowest priority)

    Args:
        project: Project containing checkpoints directory
        keep: Number of checkpoints to keep

    Returns:
        List of removed checkpoint paths
    """
    checkpoints_dir = project.checkpoints_path

    if not checkpoints_dir.exists():
        logger.debug("Checkpoints directory does not exist: {}", checkpoints_dir)
        return []

    # Get all checkpoint files
    all_ckpts = list(checkpoints_dir.glob("*.ckpt"))

    if len(all_ckpts) <= keep:
        logger.debug("Total checkpoints ({}) <= keep ({}), nothing to prune", len(all_ckpts), keep)
        return []

    # Score each checkpoint
    def score_checkpoint(ckpt: Path) -> float:
        name = ckpt.name
        if name == BEST_CKPT_NAME:
            return 2.0
        if name == FINAL_CKPT_NAME:
            return 1.5
        if name == LAST_CKPT_NAME:
            return 0.5
        return 0.0

    # Sort by score (descending), then by name for stability
    scored = sorted(all_ckpts, key=lambda p: (-score_checkpoint(p), p.name))

    # Keep the top N, remove the rest
    to_keep = scored[:keep]
    to_remove = scored[keep:]

    # Remove the files
    removed = []
    for ckpt in to_remove:
        logger.debug("Removing checkpoint: {}", ckpt)
        ckpt.unlink()
        removed.append(ckpt)

    logger.info("Pruned {} checkpoints, kept {}", len(removed), len(to_keep))
    return removed

def plot_image(img_path: Path, out_file: Path, pred_mask: NDArray[np.floating]) -> None:
    """Plot original image, predicted mask overlay, and predicted mask side by side."""
    with PILImage.open(img_path) as pil_img:
        img_rgb = pil_img.convert("RGB")
        w, h = pil_img.size

        # Ensure mask matches original size
        mask = pred_mask
        if mask.shape != (h, w):
            mask = np.array(
                PILImage.fromarray(mask).resize((w, h), resample=PILImage.Resampling.NEAREST)
            )

        # Scale figure width by number of subplots but preserve aspect
        aspect = w / h
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(3 * aspect * 3, 3))  # width ~ 3 panels

        # Input
        ax[0].imshow(img_rgb)
        ax[0].set_title("Input")
        ax[0].axis("off")

        # Overlay
        ax[1].imshow(img_rgb)
        ax[1].imshow(mask, cmap="Reds", alpha=0.4)
        ax[1].set_title("Detected Cracks (Overlay)")
        ax[1].axis("off")

        # Mask only
        ax[2].imshow(mask, cmap="gray")
        ax[2].set_title("Predicted Crackz")
        ax[2].axis("off")

        fig.tight_layout()
        # Save the plotted image
        save_detection_figure(fig, out_file)

def save_detection_figure(fig: plt.Figure, out_file: Path) -> None:
    """Save a Matplotlib figure to disk and close it safely."""
    try:
        fig.savefig(out_file, bbox_inches="tight")

            logger.debug("✅ Saved detection figure {}", out_file)

class AIDevice(Enum):
    """Available AI devices."""

    CPU = "cpu"
    CUDA = "cuda"
    MPS = "mps"  # Apple Silicon
    XLA = "xla"  # TPUs (optional)

    @staticmethod
    def available_devices() -> list["AIDevice"]:
        """Return a list of available devices on this system."""
        devices = [AIDevice.CPU]  # CPU is always available

        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            devices.append(AIDevice.CUDA)

        if getattr(torch.backends, "mps", None) and torch.backends.mps.is_available():
            devices.append(AIDevice.MPS)

        try:
            import torch_xla.core.xla_model as xm

            _ = xm.xla_device()
            devices.append(AIDevice.XLA)
        except Exception:
            logger.debug("XLA device not available")

        return devices

    @staticmethod
    def default() -> "AIDevice":
        """Return best available device, preferring GPU > MPS > CPU."""
        for dev in [AIDevice.CUDA, AIDevice.MPS]:
            if dev in AIDevice.available_devices():
                return dev
        return AIDevice.CPU

    @staticmethod
    def test_device(device_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str, dict[str, str]]:  # noqa: PLR0911
        """Test if a device is available and working.

        Args:
            device_name: Device name to test ('cpu', 'cuda', 'mps', etc.)

        Returns:
            Tuple of (success, message, details_dict) where:
            - success: True if device works
            - message: Human-readable result message
            - details_dict: Additional device information
        """
        details: dict[str, str] = {}

        try:
            # Create a test tensor on the device
            device = torch.device(device_name)

            # Use larger tensor size for GPU devices to better detect issues
            # 1000x1000 = ~4MB, representative of actual model workloads
            # but still fast enough for a UI test
            tensor_size = 1000 if device_name in {"cuda", "mps"} else 100
            test_tensor = torch.randn(tensor_size, tensor_size, device=device)

            # Perform matrix multiplication to verify device works
            # This will properly initialize GPU and test computation
            result = torch.matmul(test_tensor, test_tensor.T)
            _ = result.sum().item()  # Force computation and transfer to CPU

        except RuntimeError as e:
            error_msg = str(e)
            if "out of memory" in error_msg.lower():
                return (
                    False,
                    f"❌ Device '{device_name}' out of memory\n\nTry closing other applications.",
                    details,
                )
            if "not available" in error_msg.lower() or "not found" in error_msg.lower():
                return (
                    False,
                    f"❌ Device '{device_name}' is not available\n\n{error_msg}",
                    details,
                )
            return False, f"❌ Device test failed\n\n{error_msg}", details
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Device test failed unexpectedly")
            return False, f"❌ Unexpected error testing device\n\n{e!s}", details
        else:
            # Get device-specific details and build success message
            if device_name == "cuda":
                if not torch.cuda.is_available():
                    return False, "❌ CUDA not available on this system", details

                details["cuda_version"] = torch.version.cuda
                details["device_count"] = str(torch.cuda.device_count())
                details["device_name"] = torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)
                details["device_capability"] = ".".join(
                    map(str, torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0))
                )
                memory_allocated = torch.cuda.memory_allocated(0) / 1024**2
                memory_reserved = torch.cuda.memory_reserved(0) / 1024**2
                memory_total = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1024**2
                details["memory_allocated"] = f"{memory_allocated:.0f} MB"
                details["memory_reserved"] = f"{memory_reserved:.0f} MB"
                details["memory_total"] = f"{memory_total:.0f} MB"

                success_msg = (
                    f"✅ CUDA is working!\n\n"
                    f"GPU: {details['device_name']}\n"
                    f"CUDA Version: {details['cuda_version']}\n"
                    f"Compute Capability: {details['device_capability']}\n"
                    f"Total Memory: {details['memory_total']}\n"
                    f"Available: {memory_total - memory_reserved:.0f} MB"
                )
                return True, success_msg, details

            if device_name == "mps":
                details["backend"] = "Apple Metal Performance Shaders"
                details["pytorch_version"] = torch.__version__
                success_msg = (
                    f"✅ MPS (Apple Silicon GPU) is working!\n\n"
                    f"Backend: {details['backend']}\n"
                    f"PyTorch Version: {details['pytorch_version']}"
                )
                return True, success_msg, details

            if device_name == "cpu":
                details["cpu_count"] = str(torch.get_num_threads())
                details["pytorch_version"] = torch.__version__
                success_msg = (
                    f"✅ CPU device is working!\n\n"
                    f"Threads: {details['cpu_count']}\n"
                    f"PyTorch Version: {details['pytorch_version']}"
                )
                return True, success_msg, details

            # Generic success for other devices
            details["device_type"] = str(device.type)
            return True, f"✅ Device '{device_name}' is working!", details

def load_detection_results(project_or_path: object, *, strict: bool = False) -> DetectionResults:
    """Load detection results from JSON.

    Parameters
    ----------
    project_or_path: Project | Path | str
        Either a project instance or path to directory / file.
    strict: bool
        If True, raise ValidationError on the first invalid row.
        If False, skip invalid rows (logging a warning).
    """
    from pydantic import ValidationError

    results_file = _results_file_from_project(project_or_path)
    if not results_file.exists():  # pragma: no cover - simple guard
        return []

    raw = json.loads(results_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out: DetectionResults = []
    for entry in raw:
        try:
            out.append(DetectionResult(**entry))
        except ValidationError as e:
            if strict:
                raise
            # Late import to avoid cycle with logger at module import time
            from crackz.log.crackz_logger import logger

            logger.warning("Skipping invalid detection result row: {} -> {}", entry, e.errors())
    return out

def get_available_checkpoints(checkpoints_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """
    Get all available checkpoint files in the directory.

    Args:
        checkpoints_dir: Directory containing checkpoint files

    Returns:
        List of checkpoint paths sorted by priority (best, final, last, then others by name)
    """
    if not checkpoints_dir.exists():
        return []

    all_ckpts = list(checkpoints_dir.glob("*.ckpt"))

    # Sort by priority: best > final > last > others (alphabetically)
    def priority_key(ckpt: Path) -> tuple[int, str]:
        name = ckpt.name
        if name == BEST_CKPT_NAME:
            return (0, name)
        if name == FINAL_CKPT_NAME:
            return (1, name)
        if name == LAST_CKPT_NAME:
            return (2, name)
        return (3, name)

    return sorted(all_ckpts, key=priority_key)

def select_checkpoint(checkpoints_dir: Path) -> Path | None:
    """
    Select the best available checkpoint file in order of preference:
    1) best.ckpt
    2) last.ckpt
    3) final.ckpt.

    Args:
        checkpoints_dir: Directory containing checkpoint files

    Returns:
        Path to selected checkpoint or None if none found
    """
    best = checkpoints_dir / BEST_CKPT_NAME
    last = checkpoints_dir / LAST_CKPT_NAME
    final = checkpoints_dir / FINAL_CKPT_NAME

    if best.exists():
        logger.debug("Selected checkpoint: {} (best)", best)
        return best
    if last.exists():
        logger.debug("Selected checkpoint: {} (last)", last)
        return last
    if final.exists():
        logger.debug("Selected checkpoint: {} (final)", final)
        return final

    logger.error(
        "No checkpoint files found in {} (tried: {}, {}, {})",
        checkpoints_dir,
        best,
        last,
        final,
    )
    return None

def load_model_from_checkpoint(
    project: Project, lr: float, checkpoint_name: str | None = None
) -> CrackzModel:
    """Load a CrackzModel from the project's checkpoint directory.

    Args:
        project: Project configuration
        lr: Learning rate for the model
        checkpoint_name: Optional checkpoint name (e.g., 'best', 'last', 'epoch-0.9234').
            If None, uses automatic selection (best > last > final).
            Can be specified with or without the '.ckpt' extension.

    Returns:
        Loaded model or new untrained model if no checkpoint found
    """
    from crackz.ai.model import CrackzConfig, CrackzModel

    # If checkpoint_name is specified, use it directly
    if checkpoint_name is not None:
        # Add .ckpt extension if not present
        if not checkpoint_name.endswith(".ckpt"):
            checkpoint_name = f"{checkpoint_name}.ckpt"

        checkpoint_path = project.checkpoints_path / checkpoint_name

        if not checkpoint_path.exists():
            logger.error(
                "Specified checkpoint {} not found in {}",
                checkpoint_name,
                project.checkpoints_path,
            )
            raise ModelNotFoundError(f"Checkpoint not found: {checkpoint_path}")

        loader = CrackzModel.load_from_checkpoint
        model = loader(checkpoint_path)
        logger.info("✅ Model loaded from checkpoint {}", checkpoint_path)
        return model

    # Use automatic selection
    selected_ckpt: Path | None = select_checkpoint(project.checkpoints_path)

    if not selected_ckpt or not selected_ckpt.exists():
        logger.warning(
            "No checkpoint found in {} returning untrained model.", project.checkpoints_path
        )
        return CrackzModel(CrackzConfig.from_project(project, lr))

    loader = CrackzModel.load_from_checkpoint
    model = loader(selected_ckpt)
    logger.info("✅ Model loaded from checkpoint {}", selected_ckpt)
    return model

def create_checkpoint_callback(project: Project) -> ModelCheckpoint:
    """
    Create a ModelCheckpoint callback configured to save the best model (by val_iou)
    and the last checkpoint into the project's checkpoints directory.

    Uses project.ai.training.save_top_k and save_last configuration.

    Args:
        project: Project configuration

    Returns:
        Configured ModelCheckpoint callback
    """
    from crackz.util import ensure_dir

    checkpoints_dir = project.checkpoints_path
    ensure_dir(checkpoints_dir)

    save_last = getattr(project.ai.training, "save_last", True)

    callback = ModelCheckpoint(
        dirpath=checkpoints_dir,
        filename=CKPT_FILENAME_PATTERN,
        save_top_k=save_top_k,
        monitor="val_iou",

        save_last=save_last,
        # Add async saving to reduce memory pressure
        enable_version_counter=False,
    )

    callback.dirpath = checkpoints_dir
    return callback

def prune_checkpoints(project: Project, keep: int) -> list[Path]:
    """Prune older checkpoints, keeping only the top N based on a scoring heuristic.

    Scoring heuristic:
    - best.ckpt: score 2.0 (highest priority)
    - final.ckpt: score 1.5
    - last.ckpt: score 0.5
    - Other checkpoints: score 0.0 (lowest priority)

    Args:
        project: Project containing checkpoints directory
        keep: Number of checkpoints to keep

    Returns:
        List of removed checkpoint paths
    """
    checkpoints_dir = project.checkpoints_path

    if not checkpoints_dir.exists():
        logger.debug("Checkpoints directory does not exist: {}", checkpoints_dir)
        return []

    # Get all checkpoint files
    all_ckpts = list(checkpoints_dir.glob("*.ckpt"))

    if len(all_ckpts) <= keep:
        logger.debug("Total checkpoints ({}) <= keep ({}), nothing to prune", len(all_ckpts), keep)
        return []

    # Score each checkpoint
    def score_checkpoint(ckpt: Path) -> float:
        name = ckpt.name
        if name == BEST_CKPT_NAME:
            return 2.0
        if name == FINAL_CKPT_NAME:
            return 1.5
        if name == LAST_CKPT_NAME:
            return 0.5
        return 0.0

    # Sort by score (descending), then by name for stability
    scored = sorted(all_ckpts, key=lambda p: (-score_checkpoint(p), p.name))

    # Keep the top N, remove the rest
    to_keep = scored[:keep]
    to_remove = scored[keep:]

    # Remove the files
    removed = []
    for ckpt in to_remove:
        logger.debug("Removing checkpoint: {}", ckpt)
        ckpt.unlink()
        removed.append(ckpt)

    logger.info("Pruned {} checkpoints, kept {}", len(removed), len(to_keep))
    return removed

class CancellationToken:
    """Thread-safe cancellation token for AI workflows.

    This class allows callers to request cancellation of long-running operations
    and workers to check if cancellation has been requested.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Initialize a new cancellation token."""
        self._cancelled = threading.Event()

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        """Request cancellation of the operation."""
        self._cancelled.set()

    def is_cancelled(self) -> bool:
        """Check if cancellation has been requested.

        Returns:
            True if cancellation has been requested, False otherwise.
        """
        return self._cancelled.is_set()

    def check_cancelled(self) -> None:
        """Check if cancelled and raise exception if so.

        Raises:
            CancellationError: If cancellation has been requested.
        """
        if self.is_cancelled():
            from crackz.exceptions import CancellationError

            msg = "Operation was cancelled by user"
            raise CancellationError(msg)

class InterceptHandler(logging.Handler):
    """Redirect standard logging records to loguru."""

    def emit(self, record: LogRecord) -> None:
        """Emit a record."""
        lvl: int | str = record.levelno
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            lvl = logger.level(record.levelname).name

        frame: FrameType | None = logging.currentframe()
        depth = 2
        while frame and frame.f_code.co_filename == logging.__file__:
            frame = frame.f_back
            depth += 1

        logger.opt(depth=depth, exception=record.exc_info).log(lvl, record.getMessage())

def setup_logging(level: str | None = None, log_dir: Path | None = None) -> Logger:
    """Configure loguru + redirect stdlib logging. Safe for tests & PyInstaller."""
    settings = CrackzSettings()
    log_dir = log_dir or settings.log_dir
    if not log_dir.is_absolute():
        log_dir = Path.cwd() / log_dir
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Reset loguru handlers
    logger.remove()
    log_level = level or settings.log_level

    # Console logging
    if sys.stderr is not None:
        logger.add(
            sys.stderr,
            level=log_level,
            colorize=True,
            enqueue=True,
            backtrace=not getattr(sys, "frozen", False),
            diagnose=not getattr(sys, "frozen", False),
        )

    # File logging
    logger.add(
        str(log_dir / "crackz.log"),
        level=log_level,
        rotation="10 MB",
        retention="10 days",
        compression="zip",
        enqueue=True,
    )

    logging.basicConfig(handlers=[InterceptHandler()], level=0, force=True)

    for lib in noisy_libs:
        logging.getLogger(lib).setLevel(logging.WARNING)

    logger.debug("Logger initialized with level={}, dir={}", log_level, log_dir)
    return logger

def get_logger(name: str, filename: str | None = None, log_dir: str = "logs") -> logging.Logger:
    """Create a stdlib logger under crackz, optionally with its own FileHandler.

    Unlike loguru sinks, this uses the stdlib `logging` system directly.
    """
    _logger = logging.getLogger(f"crackz.{name}")

    if filename and not any(
        isinstance(h, logging.FileHandler) and h.baseFilename.endswith(filename)
        for h in _logger.handlers
    ):
        fh = logging.FileHandler(Path(log_dir) / filename, encoding="utf-8")
        fh.setFormatter(
            logging.Formatter(
                "%(asctime)s | %(levelname)-8s | %(name)s:%(funcName)s:%(lineno)d - %(message)s"
            )
        )
        _logger.addHandler(fh)

    return _logger

def init_project(
    name: str = NAME_OPTION,
    image_path: Path | None = IMAGE_PATH_OPTION,
    image_mask_path: Path | None = IMAGE_MASK_PATH_OPTION,
    artifacts_path: Path | None = ARTIFACTS_PATH_OPTION,
    description: str = DESCRIPTION_OPTION,
    log_dir: Path | None = LOG_DIR_OPTION,
    *,
    force: bool = FORCE_OPTION,
) -> None:
    """Initialize a new Crackz project directory and save its config."""
    project_dir = Path(name)

    # Make project_dir absolute if it's not already
    if not project_dir.is_absolute():
        project_dir = project_dir.resolve()

    # Default paths - make them absolute by combining with resolved project_dir
    image_path = image_path or (project_dir / "images")
    image_mask_path = image_mask_path or (project_dir / "masks")
    artifacts_path = artifacts_path or (project_dir / "artifacts")

    # Resolve project log dir honoring user override
    resolved_log_dir = resolve_project_log_dir(project_dir, log_dir)
    stored_log_dir = normalize_log_dir_for_config(resolved_log_dir, project_dir)

    try:
        project = create_project(
            metadata=ProjectMetadata(name=name, description=description),
            logging=LoggingConfig(log_dir=stored_log_dir, level="INFO"),
            paths=ProjectPaths(
                project_path=project_dir,
                image_path=image_path,
                image_mask_path=image_mask_path,
                artifacts_path=artifacts_path,
            ),
            force=force,
        )
        save_project(project)
        typer.secho(
            f"✅ Project '{name}' initialized. Logs at: {resolved_log_dir} "
            f"(stored as {stored_log_dir})",
            fg=typer.colors.GREEN,
        )

    except FileExistsError as e:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        typer.secho(f"Project {name} already exists", fg=typer.colors.RED)
        cli_failure(e, "Project initialization")
    except PermissionError as e:  # pragma: no cover - env specific
        cli_failure(e, "Project initialization")
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - generic catch
        cli_failure(e, "Project initialization")

def migrate_project_config(
    cfg: Path | None = CFG_OPTION,
    project_path: Path | None = PROJECT_PATH_OPTION,
    *,
    dry_run: bool = DRY_RUN_OPTION,
    no_backup: bool = NO_BACKUP_OPTION,
    migrate_files: bool = typer.Option(
        default=False,
        help="Also migrate artifacts directory structure (checkpoints to models, etc.)",
    ),
) -> None:
    """Migrate a project configuration to the current schema version.

    Automatically upgrades legacy YAML (no schema_version) by adding missing fields
    with safe defaults (e.g. ai.training.tensorboard) and stamping schema_version.

    Optionally migrates the artifacts directory structure from v2 to v3:
    - checkpoints/ to models/
    - training/tensorboard/ to runtime/tensorboard/
    - training/lightning_logs/ to runtime/lightning_logs/
    - detections/*.png to detections/visualizations/
    """
    if project_path is None and cfg is None:
        msg = "Either --project or --cfg must be specified."
        raise typer.BadParameter(msg)

    try:
        # Determine the target file to migrate
        target, project_dir = _resolve_migration_target(cfg, project_path)

        # Perform schema migration
        result = migrate_project_file(target, dry_run=dry_run, backup=not no_backup)
        status = result["status"]
        from_v = result["from_version"]
        to_v = result["to_version"]
        steps = ", ".join(result["steps"]) or "none"

        # Build message in parts to respect line length
        msg = (
            f"[{status}] {target} schema {from_v} -> {to_v} "
            f"(current={CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION}) steps: {steps}"
        )
        ok_states = {"up-to-date", "noop"}
        color = typer.colors.GREEN if status in ok_states else typer.colors.CYAN
        typer.secho(msg, fg=color)

        # Perform file migration if requested
        if migrate_files:
            _handle_file_migration(project_dir, dry_run=dry_run)

        if dry_run:
            typer.secho("Dry run complete. Rerun without --dry-run to apply.", fg=typer.colors.CYAN)

    except FileNotFoundError as e:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        cli_failure(e, "Migration")
    except ValueError as e:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        cli_failure(e, "Migration")
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - generic catch
        cli_failure(e, "Migration")

def clean_project(
    project_path: Path | None = PROJECT_PATH_OPTION,
    *,
    dry_run: bool = DRY_RUN_OPTION,
    logs_only: bool = LOGS_ONLY_OPTION,
) -> None:
    """Clean temporary files and logs from a project.

    By default, cleans logs, training artifacts, checkpoints, and detections.
    Images and masks are always preserved.
    """
    if project_path is None:
        msg = "--project must be specified."
        raise typer.BadParameter(msg)

    try:
        # Load project to get actual paths
        project = load_from_project_path_or_cfg(None, project_path)

        if dry_run:
            # Show what would be cleaned
            typer.secho("Dry run: The following would be cleaned:", fg=typer.colors.CYAN)

            # Get paths that would be cleaned
            log_dir = Path(project.logging.log_dir)
            paths_to_show = [project.tensorboard_logs_path]

            if log_dir.exists():
                paths_to_show.extend(log_dir.glob("*.log"))

            if not logs_only:
                paths_to_show.extend(
                    [
                        project.checkpoints_path,
                        project.detections_path,
                        project.training_metrics_path,
                    ]
                )

            for path in paths_to_show:
                if path.exists():
                    typer.secho(f"  • {path}", fg=typer.colors.WHITE)

            typer.secho("\nRe-run without --dry-run to apply changes.", fg=typer.colors.CYAN)
            return

        # Perform the clean using the domain method
        cleaned_count = project.clean(logs_only=logs_only)

        scope = "logs" if logs_only else "logs and artifacts"
        typer.secho(
            f"\nProject cleaned! Removed {cleaned_count} items ({scope}).",
            fg=typer.colors.BRIGHT_GREEN,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError as e:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        cli_failure(e, "Cleaning project")
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - generic catch
        cli_failure(e, "Cleaning project")

            but with suffix .png
        image_type: ImagesType
            The type/category of the images to import (ignored if split=True).
        image_size: tuple[int, int]
            Tuple specifying the width and height to resize the images.
        quality: int
            Compression quality level for the images.
        overwrite: bool
            Flag indicating whether to overwrite existing images if present.
        split: bool
            Flag to enable automatic splitting of images into train/val/test sets.
        train_ratio: float
            Ratio of images for training set when using split (default: 0.7).
        val_ratio: float
            Ratio of images for validation set when using split (default: 0.15).
        test_ratio: float
            Ratio of images for test set when using split (default: 0.15).
        random_seed: int | None
            Random seed for reproducible splits (default: None for random).

    Raises:
        typer.BadParameter:
            Raised if neither configuration nor project path is provided.
        typer.Exit:
            Raised to handle any unexpected exceptions during the process.

    Returns:
        None
    """  # noqa: E501
    if masks_source_path is None:
        masks_source_path = source_path / "masks"

    logger.info("Importing images from {}", source_path)
    logger.info("Importing masks from {}", masks_source_path)

    # Validate split ratios if split is enabled
    if split:
        split_ratio_tolerance = 0.001
        total_ratio = train_ratio + val_ratio + test_ratio
        if abs(total_ratio - 1.0) > split_ratio_tolerance:  # Allow small floating point error
            msg = f"Split ratios must sum to 1.0, got {total_ratio}"
            raise typer.BadParameter(msg)
        if train_ratio <= 0 or val_ratio < 0 or test_ratio < 0:
            msg = "Split ratios must be non-negative (train > 0)"
            raise typer.BadParameter(msg)
        logger.info(
            "Automatic split enabled: train={:.1%}, val={:.1%}, test={:.1%}",
            train_ratio,
            val_ratio,
            test_ratio,
        )

    try:
        if project_path is not None:
            project = load_project_from_path(project_path)
        elif cfg is not None:
            project = load_project(cfg)
        else:
            # Should be unreachable due to the check above; keeps type-checkers happy
            msg = "Either --project or --cfg must be specified."
            raise typer.BadParameter(msg)  # noqa: TRY301

        project = offer_migration_if_legacy(project)

        # Determine total items for progress display (simple image filter)
        exts = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".tif", ".tiff"}
        total_images = sum(
            1 for p in Path(source_path).rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in exts
        )

        masks_exts = {".png"}
        masks_total = 0
        if masks_source_path is not None:
            masks_total = sum(
                1
                for p in Path(masks_source_path).rglob("*")
                if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in masks_exts
            )

        total = total_images + masks_total
        label = (
            f"Importing ({image_type.value if hasattr(image_type, 'value') else image_type})"
            if not split
            else "Importing (auto-split)"
        )

        with tqdm.tqdm(total=total, desc=label, unit="files", ncols=100) as pbar:

            def do_progress() -> None:
                with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                    pbar.update(1)

            project.import_images(
                source_path=source_path,
                masks_source_path=masks_source_path,
                image_type=image_type,
                size=image_size,
                quality=quality,
                overwrite=overwrite,
                progress_cb=do_progress,
                split=split,
                train_ratio=train_ratio,
                val_ratio=val_ratio,
                test_ratio=test_ratio,
                random_seed=random_seed,
            )
    except Exception as e:
        cli_failure(e, "Image import")

@detect_app.command("prune-checkpoints")
def prune_checkpoints_cmd(
    keep: int = KEEP_CHECKPOINTS_OPTION,
    cfg: Path | None = CFG_OPTION,
    project_path: Path | None = PROJECT_PATH_OPTION,
) -> None:
    """Prune older checkpoints keeping only the newest/best N (heuristic)."""
    if project_path is None and cfg is None:
        msg = "Either --project or --cfg must be specified."
        raise typer.BadParameter(msg)
    try:
        project = _load_project_with_migration(cfg, project_path)
        from crackz.ai.model.checkpoints import prune_checkpoints as _prune

        removed = _prune(project, keep=keep)
        if not removed:
            typer.secho(f"No checkpoints pruned (total <= {keep}).", fg=typer.colors.CYAN)
            logger.info("No checkpoints pruned: total count <= keep {}", keep)
        else:
            typer.secho("✅ Pruned checkpoints:", fg=typer.colors.GREEN)
            for checkpoint in removed:
                typer.secho(f"  - {checkpoint.name}", fg=typer.colors.YELLOW)
            logger.info("Pruned {} checkpoints: {}", len(removed), [p.name for p in removed])
    except Exception as e:
        cli_failure(e, "Checkpoint pruning")

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: This document describes the current (implemented) architecture of Crackz, focusing on the actual code paths in this repository. Previous diagrams referenced future or hypothetical services (artifact stores, model servers, remote registries) that are not yet part of the codebase; those have been removed or clearly marked as future work.

docs.title: High-Level Overview
docs.text:
Crackz consists of two user-facing entry points sharing a common core library: - CLI (Typer) – primary automation interface (import images, train, detect, export config) - GUI (CustomTkinter) – exploratory desktop interface (project browsing, import, training & detection triggers, previews)

Core subsystems: - Project / Configuration: Pydantic models; YAML + env + defaults merged via pydantic-settings - Image Import & Layout: Normalizes images into split directories (raw/ train/ val/ test/) and masks - Dataset Layer: CrackzDataset (Torch Dataset) + DataLoader factory - Training & Detection Pipelines: PyTorch + PyTorch Lightning orchestration (training, validation, testing, inference) - Performance Utilities: Global seed, Trainer override extraction - Logging: Centralized through loguru with structured formatting - Artifacts & Outputs: Filesystem only (artifacts/models/, artifacts/runtime/, metrics JSON, detection PNGs)

No network services, model servers, remote registries, or cloud object storage are currently part of runtime behavior.

docs.title: Open Architecture & Model Flexibility
docs.text:
Crackz is built with an open architecture that supports multiple model types and use cases:

Default Configuration: Segmentation - Binary segmentation (pixel-level classification): crack/no-crack, deviation/no-deviation - Uses U-Net architecture with configurable encoder backbones (ResNet, EfficientNet, MobileNet, etc.) - Suitable for: structural crack detection, surface defect analysis, damage mapping

Alternative Model Types While segmentation is the default, the architecture supports: - Classification models: Whole-image categorization (e.g., "has crack" vs "no crack") - Multi-class segmentation: Different defect types (cracks, corrosion, spalling) - Custom architectures: Bring your own PyTorch Lightning model

Model Acquisition Workflow End users have two primary paths:

  1. Train Your Own Model
  2. Import labeled training data (images + masks)
  3. Configure model architecture and training parameters
  4. Run crackz detect train to create a custom checkpoint

  5. Ideal for: domain-specific data, unique defect types, custom requirements

  6. Use Pre-Trained Models

  7. Acquire ready-made checkpoints from model providers or partners
  8. Place checkpoint in project's artifacts/models/ directory
  9. Run crackz detect run with existing checkpoint
  10. Ideal for: quick deployment, standard use cases, proof-of-concept

Encoder Flexibility The segmentation model supports any encoder from segmentation-models-pytorch, including: - ResNet family (resnet18, resnet34, resnet50, resnet101) - EfficientNet (efficientnet-b0 through efficientnet-b7) - MobileNet (mobilenet_v2) for edge deployment - DenseNet, VGG, and many others

Configure via project.yaml: 

ai:
  model:
    encoder: resnet34        # or efficientnet-b0, mobilenet_v2, etc.
    encoder_weights: imagenet # or None for random initialization

docs.title: Common Use Cases & Model Examples
docs.text:
1. Harbor Infrastructure Inspection (Segmentation) - Task: Detect and map cracks in concrete harbor walls - Model: U-Net with ResNet34 encoder - Input: 512×512 grayscale or RGB images - Output: Binary segmentation mask highlighting crack pixels - Workflow: Train on labeled harbor images → Deploy for automated inspection

2. Bridge Surface Analysis (Multi-Class Segmentation) - Task: Identify different defect types (cracks, spalling, corrosion) - Model: U-Net with EfficientNet-B0 encoder, num_classes=3 - Input: High-resolution bridge deck photos - Output: Multi-class mask (class 1=crack, class 2=spalling, class 3=corrosion) - Workflow: Acquire pre-trained multi-defect model → Run detections on new structures

3. Quick Assessment (Classification) - Task: Rapid triage - does this image contain any cracks? - Model: Custom CNN classifier (future extension) - Input: Full-resolution photos - Output: Binary label (crack/no-crack) with confidence score - Workflow: Train lightweight classifier → Process thousands of images for filtering

4. Deviation Detection (Binary Segmentation) - Task: Identify surface irregularities or deviations from standard - Model: U-Net with MobileNetV2 (for edge deployment) - Input: Normalized surface scans - Output: Deviation mask - Workflow: Train on deviation examples → Deploy on mobile devices

5. Custom Domain Application - Task: Adapt to specific industry (e.g., aerospace panel inspection) - Model: Fine-tune from ImageNet pre-trained encoder - Input: Domain-specific imagery (composite materials, metal surfaces) - Output: Custom defect masks - Workflow: Collect small labeled dataset → Transfer learning → Production deployment

docs.title: Async Callback Architecture
docs.text: Crackz now includes an asynchronous callback infrastructure that provides Go channel-like patterns for non-blocking communication between AI operations and UI updates.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The async callback architecture solves a key performance issue: synchronous callbacks can slow down training/detection when UI updates take time to process. By using asyncio queues, we decouple AI operations from UI updates, achieving:

  • Non-blocking updates: Training/detection doesn't wait for UI rendering
  • Backpressure handling: Queues automatically manage burst updates
  • Thread-safe communication: Queue-based design works seamlessly with threading
  • Backward compatibility: Existing synchronous callbacks continue to work

docs.title: 1. CallbackDispatcher (Using Janus Queues)
docs.text:
The core component that bridges synchronous callbacks to async consumers using the janus library:

from crackz.ai.core.async_callbacks import CallbackDispatcher

dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher(maxsize=100)

# Create sync reporter for PyTorch Lightning (training thread)
progress_reporter = dispatcher.create_sync_progress_reporter()

# Use in training (synchronous context)
train(project, progress_reporter=progress_reporter)

# Consume updates asynchronously (main thread)
async for progress, message in dispatcher.iter_progress():
    update_progress_bar(progress, message)

Features: - Janus queues: Provides both sync and async interfaces to same queue - Thread-safe: Safe sync puts from training thread, async gets from main thread - Backpressure handling: Drops oldest items when queue is full - Statistics tracking: Monitor queue performance with built-in stats - Graceful shutdown: Proper cleanup with sentinel values

Why Janus? - Proper synchronization between sync/async worlds - Eliminates race conditions from manual bridging - Industry-standard solution for sync/async queue bridging

docs.title: 2. Async Consumers
docs.text:
Helper functions to create async consumers that process queue updates:

from crackz.ai.core.async_callbacks import (
    create_async_progress_consumer,
    create_async_metrics_consumer,
)

# Define callback
def update_ui(progress: float, message: str | None = None) -> None:
    progress_bar.set_value(progress)

# Create async consumer
consumer = create_async_progress_consumer(dispatcher, update_ui)

# Run in async context
await consumer()

docs.title: 3. GUI Async Helpers
docs.text:
High-level utilities for GUI integration:

from crackz.gui.async_helpers import (
    start_gui_callback_consumers,
    stop_gui_callback_consumers,
)

# Start consumers (manages event loop)
loop, tasks = start_gui_callback_consumers(
    dispatcher,
    progress_callback=update_progress,
    metrics_callback=update_metrics,
)

# ... run training ...

# Cleanup
stop_gui_callback_consumers(dispatcher, loop)

docs.title: ⚠️ GUI Thread Safety Warning
docs.text: CRITICAL: CustomTkinter/tkinter is NOT thread-safe! When using async callbacks with GUI applications, you MUST use the thread-safe wrappers:

docs.title: ❌ WRONG - Direct GUI Update
docs.text:
def on_progress(progress: float, message: str | None) -> None:
    self.progress_bar.set(progress)  # ⚠️ Called from async thread - UNSAFE!

This will cause crashes, freezes, or unpredictable behavior because the callback is invoked from the async event loop thread, not the GUI main thread.

docs.title: ✅ CORRECT - Thread-Safe Update
docs.text:
# Option 1: Manual thread-safe wrapper
def on_progress(progress: float, message: str | None) -> None:
    self.root.after(0, lambda: self.progress_bar.set(progress))

# Option 2: Use provided helper (recommended)
from crackz.gui.async_helpers import start_gui_callback_consumers

loop, tasks = start_gui_callback_consumers(
    dispatcher,
    progress_callback=update_progress,
    metrics_callback=update_metrics,
    root_widget=self.root,  # ✅ Enables automatic thread-safe wrapping
)

When you provide root_widget, the helper automatically wraps your callbacks using tkinter's thread-safe after() method.

docs.title: Pattern 1: Synchronous (Backward Compatible)
docs.text:
Existing code continues to work without changes:

def progress_callback(progress: float, message: str | None = None) -> None:
    print(f"Progress: {progress:.2%}")

train(project, progress_reporter=progress_callback)

docs.title: Pattern 2: Queue-Based (Intermediate)
docs.text:
Use dispatcher with manual async consumption:

dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher(maxsize=100)

# Create sync reporters
progress_reporter = dispatcher.create_sync_progress_reporter()
metrics_reporter = dispatcher.create_sync_metrics_reporter()

# Start training in background
training_thread = threading.Thread(
    target=train,
    args=(project,),
    kwargs={
        "progress_reporter": progress_reporter,
        "metrics_callback": metrics_reporter,
    }
)
training_thread.start()

# Consume updates asynchronously
async def consume_updates():
    async for progress, message in dispatcher.iter_progress():
        print(f"Progress: {progress:.2%} - {message}")

asyncio.run(consume_updates())

docs.title: Pattern 3: Full Async with Thread Safety (GUI - Recommended)
docs.text:
Complete async pattern for GUI applications with automatic thread safety:

from crackz.ai.core.async_callbacks import CallbackDispatcher
from crackz.gui.async_helpers import (
    start_gui_callback_consumers,
    stop_gui_callback_consumers,
)

dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher(maxsize=100)

# Start async consumers with thread-safe GUI updates
loop, tasks = start_gui_callback_consumers(
    dispatcher,
    progress_callback=self.update_progress_bar,
    metrics_callback=self.update_metrics_display,
    root_widget=self.root,  # ✅ Enables thread-safe wrapping!
)

# Create reporters
progress_reporter = dispatcher.create_sync_progress_reporter()
metrics_reporter = dispatcher.create_sync_metrics_reporter()

try:
    # Run training in background thread
    training_thread = threading.Thread(
        target=train,
        args=(project,),
        kwargs={
            "progress_reporter": progress_reporter,
            "metrics_callback": metrics_reporter,
        }
    )
    training_thread.start()
    training_thread.join()
finally:
    stop_gui_callback_consumers(dispatcher, loop)

docs.title: Without Async Callbacks (Synchronous)
docs.text:
Training Loop:
  Process batch → Update metrics → **Wait for UI** → Next batch
                                      ↑ 1-5ms overhead

For 1000 callbacks/epoch: ~4 seconds wasted waiting for UI

docs.title: With Async Callbacks (Asynchronous)
docs.text:
Training Loop:
  Process batch → Put in queue → Next batch (no wait!)
                       ↓ 0.1ms
  Async Consumer: Takes from queue → Updates UI

For 1000 callbacks/epoch: ~0.1 seconds overhead (40x faster)

docs.title: Queue Statistics & Monitoring
docs.text:
The dispatcher provides built-in statistics for monitoring queue health:

dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher(maxsize=100)

# ... use reporters ...

# Check progress queue stats
stats = dispatcher.progress_stats
print(f"Total items put: {stats.total_put}")
print(f"Total items retrieved: {stats.total_get}")
print(f"Total items dropped: {stats.total_dropped}")
print(f"Current queue size: {stats.current_size}")
print(f"Max queue size: {stats.max_size}")

# Check metrics queue stats
metrics_stats = dispatcher.metrics_stats

Use statistics to: - Monitor queue backpressure (check total_dropped) - Tune queue size based on actual usage - Identify performance bottlenecks - Debug callback issues

docs.title: Thread Safety Architecture
docs.text:
The async callback infrastructure is thread-safe by design:

  • Janus queues: Provides thread-safe sync_q for puts, async-safe async_q for gets
  • Event loop: Runs in dedicated thread with proper synchronization via threading.Event
  • GUI callbacks: Wrapped using tkinter's thread-safe after() method when using helpers
  • No busy waits: Proper event-based synchronization eliminates race conditions

Thread Flow: 

Training Thread          Async Event Loop Thread     GUI Main Thread
     │                           │                        │
     ├─ sync_q.put() ────────────>│                       │
     │  (thread-safe)             │                       │
     │                            ├─ async_q.get()        │
     │                            │                       │
     │                            ├─ root.after(0, cb) ──>│
     │                            │                       │─ Update UI

This architecture ensures: - Training never blocks on UI updates - UI updates always happen on the correct thread - No race conditions or deadlocks - Proper cleanup and shutdown

docs.title: For Existing Code
docs.text:
No changes required! Existing synchronous callbacks continue to work:

# Before (still works)
train(project, progress_reporter=my_callback)

# After (optional upgrade for better performance)
dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher()
train(project, progress_reporter=dispatcher.create_sync_progress_reporter())

docs.title: For New Code
docs.text:
Use the async pattern from the start:

from crackz.ai.core.async_callbacks import CallbackDispatcher
from crackz.gui.async_helpers import start_gui_callback_consumers

dispatcher = CallbackDispatcher(maxsize=100)
loop, tasks = start_gui_callback_consumers(
    dispatcher,
    progress_callback=update_progress,
    metrics_callback=update_metrics,
)

# Use dispatcher's sync reporters in training
train(
    project,
    progress_reporter=dispatcher.create_sync_progress_reporter(),
    metrics_callback=dispatcher.create_sync_metrics_reporter(),
)

stop_gui_callback_consumers(dispatcher, loop)

docs.text: See the module docstrings for detailed API documentation:

docs.title: Core Components (crackz.ai.core.async_callbacks)
docs.text:
• CallbackDispatcher - Main sync-to-async bridge using janus queues
  • QueueStats - Statistics dataclass for monitoring
  • create_async_progress_consumer() - Create progress consumer function
  • create_async_metrics_consumer() - Create metrics consumer function

docs.text:

  • create_threadsafe_gui_callback() - Wrap callback for thread-safe GUI updates
  • create_threadsafe_metrics_callback() - Wrap metrics callback for thread safety
  • start_gui_callback_consumers() - High-level helper to start consumers
  • stop_gui_callback_consumers() - Clean shutdown of consumers

Use help() in Python to view full API documentation:

help(CallbackDispatcher)

docs.title: Azure Batch Deployment
docs.text: This guide explains how to deploy and use Crackz on Azure Batch for distributed, scalable crack detection processing.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Azure Batch allows you to run large-scale parallel and high-performance computing (HPC) applications efficiently in the cloud. The Crackz Azure Batch deployment enables:

  • Distributed Processing: Process large datasets across multiple compute nodes
  • Scalability: Automatically scale compute resources based on workload
  • Cost Optimization: Use low-priority VMs to reduce costs
  • Container Support: Run Crackz Docker images directly on Batch nodes

Note: For smaller datasets or interactive development, consider using Azure VM deployment instead. See the VM vs Batch Comparison to help you decide which option is best for your use case.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Azure CLI: Install the Azure CLI
  2. Azure Subscription: Active Azure subscription with appropriate permissions
  3. Docker Image: Built Crackz Docker image (pushed to a container registry)
  4. Azure Login: az login to authenticate

docs.title: 1. Create a Batch Pool
docs.text:
The simplest way to create a Batch pool:

./scripts/azure/azure_batch.sh \
  --batch-account mycrackzaccount \
  --storage-account mycrackzstorage

This creates: - A Batch account named mycrackzaccount - A storage account named mycrackzstorage - A pool with 2 compute nodes (Standard_D2s_v3) - A blob container for data storage

docs.title: 2. Upload Your Data
docs.text:
Upload your Crackz project to Azure Storage:

# Get storage account key
STORAGE_KEY=$(az storage account keys list \
  --account-name mycrackzstorage \
  --resource-group subbaltica-crackz-rg \
  --query "[0].value" -o tsv)

# Upload project directory
az storage blob upload-batch \
  --account-name mycrackzstorage \
  --account-key "$STORAGE_KEY" \
  --destination crackz-data \
  --source ./my-project

docs.title: 3. Submit a Job
docs.text:
Create and submit a Batch job:

# Create job
az batch job create \
  --id crackz-detection-job \
  --pool-id crackz-pool

# Add tasks to the job
az batch task create \
  --job-id crackz-detection-job \
  --task-id detect-task-1 \
  --command-line "docker run crackz-cli:latest detect run --project /mnt/batch/tasks/fsmounts/crackz-data/my-project"

docs.title: Pool Configuration
docs.text: Option Description Default --batch-account Azure Batch account name (required) - --resource-group Azure resource group name subbaltica-crackz-rg --location Azure region swedencentral --pool-id Unique pool identifier crackz-pool --vm-size VM size for compute nodes Standard_D2s_v3 --node-count Number of dedicated nodes 2 --image Docker image to use crackz-cli:latest --storage-account Storage account for data - --container Blob container name crackz-data

docs.title: VM Sizes for Different Workloads
docs.text:
VM Size vCPUs Memory Use Case Hourly Cost* Standard_D2s_v3 2 8 GB Small datasets, testing ~$0.10 Standard_D4s_v3 4 16 GB Medium datasets ~$0.20 Standard_D8s_v3 8 32 GB Large datasets ~$0.40 Standard_NC6s_v3 6 112 GB GPU acceleration (V100) ~$3.06 Standard_NC4as_T4_v3 4 28 GB GPU acceleration (T4) ~$0.53

* Approximate costs as of 2024, subject to change

docs.title: Custom Pool Configuration
docs.text:
Create a pool with custom settings:

./scripts/azure/azure_batch.sh \
  --batch-account crackz-batch \
  --pool-id high-performance-pool \
  --vm-size Standard_D8s_v3 \
  --node-count 10 \
  --storage-account crackzstore

docs.title: GPU-Enabled Pool
docs.text:
For GPU acceleration, use GPU-capable VM sizes:

./scripts/azure/azure_batch.sh \
  --batch-account crackz-batch-gpu \
  --pool-id gpu-pool \
  --vm-size Standard_NC4as_T4_v3 \
  --node-count 2 \
  --image crackz-cli:gpu

docs.title: Auto-Scaling Pools
docs.text:
For dynamic workloads, configure auto-scaling by modifying the pool after creation:

# Enable auto-scaling
az batch pool autoscale enable \
  --pool-id crackz-pool \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount \
  --auto-scale-formula '
    startingNumberOfVMs = 2;
    maxNumberofVMs = 10;
    pendingTaskSamplePercent = $PendingTasks.GetSamplePercent(180 * TimeInterval_Second);
    pendingTaskSamples = pendingTaskSamplePercent < 70 ? startingNumberOfVMs : avg($PendingTasks.GetSample(180 * TimeInterval_Second));
    $TargetDedicatedNodes = min(maxNumberofVMs, pendingTaskSamples);
  '

docs.title: Batch Processing Multiple Projects
docs.text:
Process multiple crack detection projects in parallel:

#!/bin/bash
# Create job
az batch job create --id multi-project-job --pool-id crackz-pool

# Submit tasks for each project
for project in project1 project2 project3; do
  az batch task create \
    --job-id multi-project-job \
    --task-id "detect-$project" \
    --command-line "docker run crackz-cli:latest detect run --project /data/$project"
done

docs.title: Training and Detection Pipeline
docs.text:
Run a complete training and detection pipeline:

# Training task
az batch task create \
  --job-id pipeline-job \
  --task-id train \
  --command-line "docker run crackz-cli:latest detect train --project /data/my-project --epochs 50"

# Detection task (depends on training)
az batch task create \
  --job-id pipeline-job \
  --task-id detect \
  --depends-on train \
  --command-line "docker run crackz-cli:latest detect run --project /data/my-project"

docs.title: Batch Job with Output Files
docs.text:
Configure tasks to upload outputs back to storage:

az batch task create \
  --job-id output-job \
  --task-id detect-with-output \
  --command-line "docker run -v /mnt/output:/output crackz-cli:latest detect run --project /data/project" \
  --resource-files '[{"httpUrl":"https://mystorage.blob.core.windows.net/input/data.zip","filePath":"data.zip"}]' \
  --output-files '[{"filePattern":"/mnt/output/**/*","destination":{"container":{"containerUrl":"https://mystorage.blob.core.windows.net/results"}},"uploadOptions":{"uploadCondition":"taskCompletion"}}]'

docs.title: Check Pool Status
docs.text:
az batch pool show \
  --pool-id crackz-pool \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount \
  --query "{State:allocationState, DedicatedNodes:currentDedicatedNodes}"

docs.title: List Running Jobs
docs.text:
az batch job list \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount \
  -o table

docs.title: Monitor Task Progress
docs.text:
az batch task list \
  --job-id crackz-detection-job \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount \
  -o table

docs.title: Get Task Logs
docs.text:
az batch task file download \
  --job-id crackz-detection-job \
  --task-id detect-task-1 \
  --file-path stdout.txt \
  --destination ./task-stdout.txt \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount

docs.title: Using Low-Priority VMs
docs.text:
Low-priority VMs can reduce costs by up to 80%:

# After pool creation, modify to use low-priority nodes
az batch pool resize \
  --pool-id crackz-pool \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount \
  --target-dedicated-nodes 0 \
  --target-low-priority-nodes 4

Note: Low-priority VMs may be preempted, so ensure your tasks are resilient.

docs.title: Pool Management
docs.text:
Delete pools when not in use:

./scripts/azure/azure_batch.sh \
  --batch-account mycrackzaccount \
  --pool-id crackz-pool \
  --destroy

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text: Issue Solution Pool creation fails Check quota limits: az batch location quotas show --location <region> Tasks stuck in "Running" Check task logs: az batch task file download Container image not found Ensure image is in an accessible registry Authentication errors Run az batch account login before operations

docs.title: Debug Task Failures
docs.text:
# Get task details
az batch task show \
  --job-id crackz-detection-job \
  --task-id detect-task-1 \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount

# Download stderr
az batch task file download \
  --job-id crackz-detection-job \
  --task-id detect-task-1 \
  --file-path stderr.txt \
  --destination ./task-stderr.txt \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount

docs.title: Increase Batch Quotas
docs.text:
If you hit quota limits, request an increase:

# Check current quotas
az batch location quotas show --location swedencentral

# Submit quota increase request through Azure Portal
# Support > New support request > Issue type: Service and subscription limits

docs.title: GitHub Actions Example
docs.text:
name: Azure Batch Processing
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  batch-process:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Azure Login
        uses: azure/login@v1
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Batch Pool
        run: |
          ./scripts/azure/azure_batch.sh \
            --batch-account ${{ secrets.BATCH_ACCOUNT }} \
            --storage-account ${{ secrets.STORAGE_ACCOUNT }}

      - name: Submit Batch Job
        run: |
          az batch job create --id ci-job-${{ github.run_number }} --pool-id crackz-pool
          az batch task create \
            --job-id ci-job-${{ github.run_number }} \
            --task-id detect \
            --command-line "docker run crackz-cli:latest detect run --project /data/project"

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use Managed Identities: Avoid storing credentials in code
  2. Private Container Registries: Use Azure Container Registry with authentication
  3. Network Isolation: Deploy pools in Virtual Networks
  4. Encryption: Enable encryption for storage accounts
  5. RBAC: Use role-based access control for Batch resources

docs.title: Optimize Task Slots
docs.text:
Adjust taskSlotsPerNode for better resource utilization:

# Modify pool to allow multiple tasks per node
az batch pool set \
  --pool-id crackz-pool \
  --account-name mycrackzaccount \
  --json-file pool-config.json

Where pool-config.json contains: 

{
  "taskSlotsPerNode": 4
}

docs.title: Batch Size Configuration
docs.text:
For detection tasks, adjust batch size based on VM memory:

VM Size Recommended Batch Size Notes Standard_D2s_v3 (8 GB) 4-8 Conservative for 512x512 images Standard_D4s_v3 (16 GB) 16-32 Good balance Standard_D8s_v3 (32 GB) 32-64 Large batches

Modify project configuration before uploading:

ai:
  detection:
    batch_size: 16  # Adjust based on VM size
